review_body:
Here is my two cents on Potensic. I had my hopes up for this drone. It was a lot of bang for the bucks o I took a chance. I ordered the Atom 2 fly more package. Well, when it arrived I was very impressed. It seemed very well built. It really looded good for another mini drone. I charged it up, which didn't take to long in their propriatory charger. The bag was as expected. But the controller was something different. Dog bone style. Your monitor goes in between the handles. Controlls were a little backwards, but can be changed.
Time for the first flight. This little drone was very impressive. Liftoff it went straight up and hovered tightly. I flew it around and really started to like this one. Videoing in night mode is great. It had all of the bells and whistles. It flew very nice. It takes very good pictures and videos.
After several days the only thing that botherd me was no nd filters. Yes, you could use ones made for other drones, but to me they never really fit right. But they have fixed that now if you can get your hands on one.
So here I have an excellent drone. I flew it almost every day waiting for it to fall apart. No such thing. Even after a few "hard landings" the drone performed great. Untill.....I really goofed. I broke an arm and the camera gimbal was all out of wack. So I get intouch with Potensic. Things seemed to go slow, but they are across the world and are working when I am in bed. And boy am I glad that I bought the extended warrenty that they offer. It took about two weeks because they would ask for something and I would not get that until the morning. By the time that I replyed, it was all ready the next morning before I would get anotyer reply back. BUT, they did an outstanding Job at getting me a new drone once everything they asked me to do failed.

So GREAT job for making a fantastic little drone. And GREAT job on the warranty work, even if it took a little time. I am very impressed, and I think anyone ordering the Atom 2 will be too.

review_body: This is the first drone I have bought since 2014 and I am really impressed with the technology and features this drone has. First, the stability is impressive, and it hovers in position well even with about 15 MPH winds. Second, the picture (48 megapixel) and video (4K/30 fps) quality can be compared to a high-end DSLR camera. The different camera modes and settings are helpful in taking good pictures and videos. Third, the return to home and intelligent flight modes made it easy for beginners to operate this drone. Fourth, the PTD1 RC eliminates the need to use a phone or tablet to operate this drone. Finally, there is a big difference between this drone and the last drone I bought in 2014, night and day differences (ease of flying, camera quality, video quality, different flight modes, etc.). There are two things I don’t like about this drone. First, Potensic requires account creation, activation, and registration before you can fly the drone even with the PTD1 RC. Additionally, warranty offers kept showing up on the PTD1 screen every time I turned the controller on. Luckily, it stopped popping up after a few days. Second thing I don’t like about this drone is that the batteries don’t hold charge well. Even when not in use, I have to charge the batteries weekly or they will be fully drained. Overall, it’s a descent drone and I can honestly recommend it.

review_title: This is a fabulous drone with lots of features at a great price.
review_body:
This Potensic Atom 2 drone is super fun and really easy to fly. The 4K video is awesome—super clear and sharp, whether you’re flying in daylight or at night with decent lighting. I weighed it on my kitchen scale with the batteries, and it’s about 250 grams, even with a few Velcro stickers I stuck on for some nighttime LEDs.
I’ve flown this thing in some pretty strong winds, like class 4 or 5, and it held up great. It even gave me motor warnings once, but the video stayed steady when hovering. In heavy winds, the video can get a bit shaky, but this drone does a solid job keeping itself stable. It’s rated for class 5 winds, and I believe it. I flew it a full mile line of sight, and my remote still had three bars of signal—pretty impressive for a small drone.
Now, a quick heads-up: always check your airspace. I live near a naval base, and helicopters fly low, like 200 feet above me. The drone’s noise isn’t too bad, and just so you know, it doesn’t record sound with the video.
Okay, here’s the good and the bad. Bad news: this drone doesn’t like water. I messed up and got it stuck in a tree, and it fell into a river for like 10 seconds. Good news: it’s flying fine now! I pulled the battery out right away, dried it out for a couple of days on my air purifier set to high, and it was good to go a week later. Sadly, the battery that got wet is toast, but I’d rather lose a $50 battery than a $400 drone. If you ever get it in saltwater, rinse it with fresh water first to avoid corrosion.
Overall, this drone is a blast and super easy to use. Watch a few videos to get the hang of the features, check the propeller screws, and do your calibrations. It’s basic stuff, but it keeps things safe. This little drone is small but packs a punch!

review_title: Some not so good initial observations about the Potensic Atom 2 (Yes, I test drones!)
review_body:
**** UPDATE: Waypoints, although initially advertised as included, then later they said would be added in a future update, have apparently been scrapped and WILL NOT be added! Potensic have deceived customers who made a buying decision based on this feature. Instead they added lame Cineroll and Pano-sphere features (gimmicks). They could have at least carried the waypoints function over from the previous Atom instead of ditching it! ****

Firstly, I am disappointed that the updated app (Potensic Eve) for this drone STILL DOES NOT HAVE MPH (miles per hour) as the unit of Speed when Imperial units are selected, like the previous Potensic Pro app did. Instead it uses ft/sec. Here in the US we measure speeds in mph, NOT ft/sec. Why on earth did they take that away? They could at least provide it as an option (mph or ft/sec) like they did for metric (km/h or m/s). Sorry, Potensic but this is an unacceptable blunder that you have been told about numerous times by myself and others. You need to fix it ASAP! Should be easy. Have your app programmers look at how it was in the previous version app.
Also, the telemetry data (D, H, VD, VH) should use a BIGGER character size (we’re not all young with perfect vision!) and be located at the bottom of the screen (like in the previous version app).
Also, telemetry data units (ft, ft/s) are tiny and too high up. They should be bigger and immediately to the right of the numbers.
Also, the telemetry data (D, H, VD, VH) jumps back and forth as the numbers change. Would be better to use the stacked format at bottom of screen like in the previous version app.
Also, because telemetry data is at top of screen, in white text, it is hard to see against light blue sky or white cloudy sky background, especially as it is so small! Again, would be better at bottom of screen.

As the number of satellites changes (such as between 20 and 21) the camera tilt angle and satellite icons jump left & right. Annoying! Didn’t they test this?

Potensic advertises the Atom 2 as having Waypoints, but IT DOES NOT! The previous version did and, although basic point-to-point, I used it. They could have carried over the previous version’s waypoints as a stop-gap instead of taking that function away completely. Many Atom 2 owners in the “Official” Potensic Atom group on Facebook have complained about this missing feature but Potensic have remained silent about when, or even if, it will be reinstated.
UPDATE: Potensic responded denying that they ever claimed the Atom 2 would include waypoints. That is NOT true! They are also saying that there are NO plans to add waypoints. In other words, they've back-tracked.

Camera is still only 30fps at 4K resolution. It really should be 60fps. I don’t want to have to decrease the resolution below 4K to get 60fps. There is also no way that I’ve found to adjust camera settings. The video quality is very good though.

Uses same batteries and charging hub as previous Atom, which is good. Previous version’s carry case won’t accommodate newer controller though. New controller is bigger and heavier than the previous version. I’m sorry to say that I prefer smaller and lighter. It does have some extra function buttons though. But....I'm disappointed that it is
It is STILL necessary to use an extension cable to use a tablet as the included cable (proprietary) is not long enough and one-piece, third-party cables won’t work with the controller. They could have made the included cable a little longer (by one measly inch, how hard could that have been!) so as not to need an extension cable. Or they could have moved the USB socket on the bottom of the controller 1-2" to the right as most tablets have their USB socket on the bottom (faces to right when rotated). Don't their designers think and test? Its not like there haven’t been many, many complaints about this for the previous Atom! I wish Potensic would pay attention to its owners and address their commonly reported issues!

Drone icon does not stay centered in bottom left mini-map window. It goes off the edge so is hard to see the green signal strength triangle. This was a common complaint with the previous version app. It should remain centered. Also why is the mini-map now square when it was previously rectangular and showed more area!

SD card is hard to remove because of the battery retaining clip.

I accidentally turned controller off with my thumb joint that briefly pressed the power button resulting in loss of connection! Should require short then long press to turn off. When I turned it back on I had to go through the initial pairing and excessive warning messages during which time the drone entered RTH mode and I was flying blind!

Repeated wind warnings very annoying. Unable to dismiss or mute them. Lots of other annoying warnings and messages too! I don't need to keep being told I've reached maximum height of 393ft. It's a perfectly legal height! Don’t need all that screen clutter on takeoff either. I want to be able to see what I’m doing, not dismissing unnecessary messages and warnings!

When tilting camera all the way down then back up again the camera image in the app screen pixelates.

After cancelling RTH it reverts to initial default at takeoff, rather than what was in effect prior to RTH kicking in. So if I take off with the default (V), then switch to N, then S in flight, and RTH mode kicks in, it goes back to V when RTH is cancelled. Should really go back to S.

Drops out of Sport mode to Normalwhen battery level drops below 30%. Highest speed is then only 25ft/sec (17mph) which makes for a very slow return from 1-2 miles away! Even in Sport mode the Atom 2 is slower than the previous Atom 3-axis. Plus it cam barely ascend (very slowly) while flying forward at full speed! You must first stop if you need to ascend rapidly. Weaker motors perhaps.

When distance > 9,999ft the units change from feet to miles. I don't want that, I want feet like in previous version app (and other drones). For example: 10,000ft.

Managed to fly over 2 miles (each way) with a few RC disconnecs and video freezes..

Battery level is impossible to read against background, especially in bright sunlight, when it drops to 10% and below because it is Red text on a transparent dark background. Such a ridiculous color choice! You need to see the battery level when it is getting critical. Didn’t Potensic test this app before release? Seems not!

The method for selecting Quick Shots is rather obscure! AI is just hype! Circles aren’t very circular/smooth. Spirals also aren’t very smooth. Boomerangs are circles with height change (should be elliptical/oval with a 2:1 aspect ratio). Did they even test this?
Also, should default to AI Quick Shots rather than AI Track if that is what I keep choosing by default.

The path color used in the flight viewer is useless against background that it is green or brown fields of grass in Satellite mode (White or Light Blue would be better).
Flight viewer provides no indication of which Quick Shot has been invoked and is in effect.
No way to delete unwanted flight records.

Unfortunately this drone is spoiled by the terrible presentation of the telemetry data (font size too small, badly located, poor choice of colors, no mph units, jumps to L & R as numbers change, miles instead of thousands of feet if > 9,999ft, units too tiny).

Sorry Potensic but this new Eve app has been very badly developed and poorly tested relative to the previous Pro app which was MUCH better. The developers and testers should be ashamed of it! Didn’t they test it in real-world situations? They get 5/10 or a C grade!

I wish it were possible to use the previous Potensic Pro app with the Atom 2 as it was MUCH better than the new, buggy, poorly tested Eve app!

NOTE: I also have a Potensic Atom 3-axis drone so have it for comparison. I became unhappy with it after a firmware update earlier this year adversely affected its range. There were many complaints about this in the “Official” Potensic Atom group on Facebook but Potensic ignored the complaints and have refused address the problem. Maybe their goal was to drive people to the newer Atom 2.
I also own a DJI Mini 3, Mini 4K and HS900.
The Atom 2 doesn't come close to the DJI Mini 3 or even the Mini 4K

review_body:
I've been flying drones for a couple of years now, and the Potensic Atom 2 has quickly become my favorite for everyday adventures. At under 249g, it's incredibly lightweight and portable – no need for FAA registration, and it folds up small enough to slip into my pocket or daypack without any hassle.
The camera setup is where this drone shines: a 1/2" Sony CMOS sensor captures stunning 48MP (8K) photos and smooth 4K/30fps HDR videos, all stabilized by a reliable 3-axis gimbal. The colors are vibrant, details are sharp even in low light thanks to the F1.8 aperture, and features like vertical shooting make it perfect for creating social media content on the fly. I love the QuickShots modes – like Orbit and Follow Me – which add that cinematic flair without much effort.
Battery life is impressive at up to 32 minutes per charge, giving me plenty of time to explore and capture footage. The GPS positioning is spot-on, with return-to-home working flawlessly every time, even in moderate winds. Transmission range is solid too, keeping the feed clear and responsive.
It doesn't have obstacle avoidance, but that's actually a plus in my book – it keeps the drone sleek, affordable, and focused on core flying fun, helping me build better piloting skills along the way. For beginners or anyone wanting high-quality aerial shots without breaking the bank, the Atom 2 is an absolute gem. Highly recommend – it's punched way above its weight class!

Muy buena calidad de imagen, muy ligero y pequeño. Perfecto para uso recreativo. Las instrucciones visuales que vienen en la App son muy útiles y se agradecen para la gente que nunca ha usado un dron antes, en mi caso soy principiante y nunca he usado antes uno y es bastante sencillo de entender todo. Eso si recomiendo mirar videos de youtube u otras aplicaciones donde enseñan diferentes trucos y formas de uso.

After 23 flights, I can say the Atom-2 is stable, reliable, and has good video. It's very easy to take off and land manually. Return to Home works very well. The maximum range I've flown is 2-1/2 miles and 360 feet high - no glitches with video or control. If you aren't pointing the antenna toward the drone, the RF signal bars turn red as a good reminder.
I had only one problem initially, flying very low over a crop of soybeans (about 5 feet above them, 20 feet away from me) .. I stepped behind a vehicle from the front to the back with the remote, holding it above the roofline .. shortly after that the connection was lost and the drone did the automatic RTH. I was advised by Support not to fly very low, the signal will be better higher up.
The stated battery life 20 minutes is about right, in any case it's plenty of time to take video shots while flying over a wide area. I only had one incident of allowing the battery voltage to get too low .. the drone was almost back to my landing spot when it suddenly announced it was 'landing now' and did just that.
The video quality is great, I use mostly 25 fps and 1080p in Auto mode. Panning quickly (rotating the drone) produces a jerky-video effect though, so I rotate the drone slowly and rely more on dolly and zoom shots for best quality. The digital zoom feature produces very bad/fuzzy video, I haven't found a good use for it yet.
Customer support has been very good, they respond quickly and accurately.

Ich habe die Potensic ATOM 2 Drohne jetzt zwei Tage intensiv getestet – bei unterschiedlichen Lichtverhältnissen, Windbedingungen und mit allen Features, die sie bietet – und ich bin ehrlich begeistert. Ich hatte vorher das Vorgängermodell Atom 1 (bzw. 4K) Diese Drohne ist eine echte Überraschung – im positiven Sinne.
Positiv:
✅ Perfekt für Anfänger & Profis:
Die Drohne ist super einsteigerfreundlich – auspacken, alles ist sicher verstaut in der sehr hochwertigen Tasche, Akku laden, App installieren – und los geht’s. Gleichzeitig bietet sie auch für erfahrene Piloten genug Funktionen, um richtig Spaß zu haben.
✅ Keine Registrierung notwendig:
Mit unter 249 Gramm fällt die ATOM 2 in die C0-Kategorie – somit ist kein Drohnenführerschein notwendig, was gerade für Hobbyflieger ein großer Pluspunkt ist.
✅ Fliegt sich wie von selbst:
Die Steuerung ist präzise, intuitiv und zuverlässig. Selbst bei leichtem Wind steht die Drohne stabil in der Luft. Die Verbindung zur Fernbedienung bleibt auch bei größerer Entfernung stabil – die 10km Reichweitehabe ich jetzt nicht getestet, da der Flug ja nur im Sichtbereich erlaubt ist. Aber da alles TOP!
✅ 4K HDR & 8K Fotos – Wahnsinnig gute Bildqualität:
Was mich wirklich beeindruckt hat, ist die Kamera. Die 3-Achsen-Gimbal-Stabilisierung liefert extrem ruhige Aufnahmen. Die Fotos in 8K sind gestochen scharf, und auch HDR-Videos sehen fantastisch aus.
✅ AI-Funktionen wie „Follow Me“, „QuickShots“ & Nachtmodus:
Die intelligenten Flugmodi funktionieren tadellos. Besonders „Follow Me“ war eine Freude – die Drohne bleibt zuverlässig dran, selbst bei flotterem Gehen oder leichtem Joggen. Der AI-Nachtmodus ist erstaunlich gut – ich hatte wirklich nicht erwartet, dass bei so wenig Licht noch so detailreiche Aufnahmen entstehen. Da hat Potensic ein definitiv starkes Feature nachgebessert im Vergleich zum Vorgängermodell ATOM 1.
✅ Fly More Combo = Mega Deal:
Ich habe die Fly More Combo gekauft – mit drei Akkus (insgesamt rund 96 Minuten Flugzeit) und einer tollen Tasche. Für den Preis einfach unschlagbar. Wenn man sich vergleichbare Modelle bei DJI anschaut, zahlt man schnell deutlich mehr.
✅ Fernbedienung = Riesen-Upgrade zum Vorgänger:
Die neue Fernbedienung liegt perfekt in der Hand, ist wertig verarbeitet und super responsiv. Hier hat Potensic wirklich einen großen Schritt nach vorne gemacht.
✅ Ernsthafte DJI-Konkurrenz im unteren Preissegment:
Ich hätte es nicht gedacht, aber Potensic ist in diesem Preisbereich definitiv auf Augenhöhe mit DJI – wenn nicht sogar einen Tick voraus, wenn man das Gesamtpaket betrachtet.
Neutral:
➖ Akkulaufzeit realistisch ca. 25 Min.
Angegeben sind bis zu 32 Minuten Flugzeit – das erreicht man vermutlich nur bei perfekten Bedingungen ohne Wind. In meinem Test kam ich je nach Flugweise auf ca. 23–26 Minuten pro Akku, was absolut in Ordnung ist.
Negativ:
⚠️ Keine Hinderniserkennung:
Das ist der einzige Punkt, der vielleicht als Schwäche gesehen werden kann. Aber ganz ehrlich – in dieser Preisklasse gibt’s das bei keiner Drohne, und wenn man weiß, was man tut, ist es kein Problem. Wer auf Nummer sicher gehen will, fliegt halt etwas vorsichtiger.
Fazit:
Die Potensic ATOM 2 hat mich wirklich positiv überrascht. Top Verarbeitung, super Bildqualität, intelligente Flugmodi und eine tolle Fernbedienung – alles in einem Paket, welches auch erschwinglich ist. Für mich ist sie aktuell die beste Einsteigerdrohne mit Profi-Anspruch unter 500 Euro. Ich freue mich jetzt schon auf die nächsten Flüge – das Ding macht einfach Spaß!

It is a DJI micro drone for beginners. But not for kids. What is a micro drone? One with a weight below 250g. In this case, you are not required to get a license to use it. The mini 4K is a light version of the DJI mini 4, great to learn and light on your pocket if you crash it (without insurance). This is my first drone. I have to admit - I expected more from the camera, especially in low light. But it is expected. You cannot get the same quality images and videos as from the DJI mini 4 Pro. It is a different class. Flying the drone for the first time is a bit challenging. First, make sure you learn the regulations and understand that flying is a privilege, not a right. Download the NAV Drone Canada app, create an account, and learn about the rules in your area (or the area you want to fly over).
A drone combo makes a lot of sense, especially when you get a good deal. Otherwise, you'll pay more for the drone and accessories. Also, buy a hard case. The bag included with the kit is good, but not protective enough. Buy extra batteries, but good ones (don't take risks with poor quality batteries). Don't spend too much on accessories that you don't know how to use. If you plan to learn, no problem. For example, filters. If you know their role and importance, fine - get 'em! Also, don't buy accessories that will push the weight of your drone to or above the 250g limit, because you'll risk entering a different category governed by different rules.
My drone works fine and gave me a great opportunity to learn. Some of you may be tempted to buy the DJI Neo because it's cheaper and easier to use. I'd say the price isn't too different in the end. With accessories in a kit similar to this one, the price becomes irrelevant. The rest is... different! The DJI Neo is great for vloggers, mostly interested in the ability of the drone to follow its owner. The noise, the range, and controlling it are very different. The DJI mini 4K is closer to a real drone for photographers and videographers. It has some predefined (quick) flight patterns that can help you, but, to most of us disappointing, no tracking! You really want this drone to learn real flying using the remote control (and not your phone, except as a viewing screen).
I'm having fun with this drone, and I suggest everyone take it slowly in Cinematic Mode (later in Normal Mode), learning the basic movements, experimenting in open areas like a school football field early in the morning or late in the afternoon, without bothering people, keeping your distance and your eyes on the drone. Don't jump to long and complicated flights too quickly. Do not rely on obstacle avoidance. The Sport Mode disables the obstacle avoidance anyway. This drone has a limited ability to avoid them, especially in low visibility. DJI mini 4K is not waterproof. Do not fly in the rain or fog. It may fail. Do not fly over the water if you didn't learn how to fly really well. Do not rely on the battery lasting the specified time (usually calculated in ideal conditions). If it's windy, if you are an aggressive pilot, if the battery wasn't fully charged to begin with, consider 50...60% of the 30-minute time suggested by the specs. The drone has the return home ability, but not without enough juice in the battery.
My first flight was a straight up and down line. As simple as possible. Keep it low for a while (20..30 meters above your head). Just look around through your camera and learn to point it ahead and down at various degrees. Learn to rotate the drone clockwise and counterclockwise from a steady position. Learn more complicated flight movements around you in a range of 30...50 meters. Keep your eyes on the drone and learn to use the remote without looking for the controls. It would be great to learn to fly on a simulator first until you feel comfortable with the controls.
In conclusion, be wise and take it slowly. If you can, go to a drone flight school or have a trained pilot teach you a thing or two. Don't forget: the greatest disappointment is not to crash your drone (because you will) but to crash an expensive one because you didn't learn on a cheaper one first. And, once again: follow all the rules and regulations even if you fly a micro drone for recreation. In the end, it's not about you but the safety of others. Have fun!

I’m really impressed with this drone so far! The first thing I noticed was how well everything was packaged. It comes with a sturdy carrying case that keeps all the accessories organized and makes it easy to take anywhere. The drone folds up into a compact size, so it doesn’t take up much space, and the build quality feels solid. The GPS positioning works well, the drone is stable in the air, and the controls are responsive. The video quality is clear, and it’s easy to learn and a lot of fun to fly. Overall, this is a great choice for beginners or anyone looking for a portable drone. It would also make an excellent gift because the packaging is attractive and everything is neatly organized. Highly recommended!

I’m very impressed with this drone! It was easy to set up, and the GPS feature makes flying much more stable and beginner-friendly. The remote controller with the built-in screen is convenient because I don’t need to use my phone.
The drone is lightweight, folds up nicely, and comes with a quality carrying case that keeps everything organized. The battery life is good for casual flying, and the controls are responsive. The camera quality is decent for the price and captures clear photos and videos in good lighting.
Overall, this is an excellent value for anyone looking for an affordable GPS drone. Highly recommended for beginners and hobbyists alike!

I am very impressed with this GPS drone. It is easy to set up, stable in the air, and beginner-friendly. The built-in screen on the controller is convenient because I do not need to connect my phone. The camera produces clear, smooth footage, and the EIS helps reduce shaking. GPS return-to-home works reliably, giving me extra confidence while flying. I’m very impressed with this GPS drone! It’s lightweight (under 249g), making it easy to carry and fly. I’m really impressed with this drone! It was very easy to set up and fly, even for a beginner. The GPS auto return feature gives me extra confidence, and the flight is stable thanks to the EIS camera system.

I’m very happy with this drone! It was easy to set up and fly, even for a beginner. The camera quality is clear, and the flight is smooth and stable. The battery life is good, and the controller is very responsive.

I am very satisfied with this drone. It was easy to set up and operate from the first flight. The camera offers good image and video quality, and the GPS helps maintain a stable flight. For the price, it offers very good functions and is an excellent option for both beginners and those looking for a good quality drone without spending too much. This Ruko U11MINI has me blown away for so many reasons. The picture and video quality is not lacking at all, very surprised with the quality of the camera in all lighting conditions. I think my favorite thing about this drone is that its under 250 grams so I don't have to worry about going through government registration!! Great drone for the price. Very easy to fly, my son has pretty severe cerebral palsy and he can fly it well. Stable even in wind, hovers right where you leave it. Very good camera with great resolution, it even pivots up and down to get angle you need, adjustment is on controller. Camera has been upgraded and is very stable, even with windy wobbly flight. The setup and getting started process with the Ruko U11 Mini is incredibly simple. What an amazing drone! At first I was a little skeptical but ordered based on the reviews, and it turned out to be so nice. Loved how it can connect to a phone and record in 4K. This drone exceeds every expectation I had for it the quality is amazing the size is small but rugged great for beginners and experts alike the carrying case is great quality the video quality is astonishing this thing is fun fast and could be used as a professional video drone

This is a review for the Potensic ATOM 3-Axis Gimbal 4K GPS Drone, Under 249g, 96 Mins Flight
This drone is absolutely fantastic for the price. This performs just as well as the more well known brands at a serious discount. The GPS features, camera modes, and inbuilt stabilization actually make this much easier to fly than those less expensive drones. The drone itself is very quick, and captures stabilized video in fantastic quality. That fantastic quality is topped off by being controlled by an onboard gimble, meaning you can look at things from all sorts of angles, point it almost straight down to check out your roof, or up high to get some fantastic cinematic shots.
Though I'm kind of loathe to say this, I dropped this drone the very second I unpackaged it and it shrugged off the hit like I had done nothing to it. I'm used to such accidents snapping props and all sorts of chaos on less expensive drones, but this guy right here is very, very durable.
While I think the 6KM range is a bit of a stretch, this drone does have a long range, and it's very easy to accidentally go beyond visual range because you typically get rock solid video from the unit. The included soft case is fantastic for bringing your drone wherever you want; typically I stash it in my car where it's basically invisible.
This was my first "Serious" drone, and honestly, it's so much easier to fly than those cheaper ones. The best way to describe the difference is that one cheaper drones, the vertical controls control the speed of your props, and the height will be variable depending on external factors. For drones of this class, the vertical controls set your height, and the onboard computer takes care of the variable factors for you.
I liked flying drones before, but now I LOVE flying. What you get for the price in this set is fantastic.

Bought the Atom over a year and a half ago. I flew it maybe 3-4 times in the first month since it was winter time and super cold out.
Then life got busy, and I forgot I even had this thing until this past weekend, I finally broke it out of the box again.
Man is thing is impressive. Especially for the price point. Best value for your dollar out there.
It’s super easy to fly, even for someone with little to no experience with flying quadcopters/drones. My 6 year old figured it out in about 3 mins.
Camera and video quality are fantastic. Takes great photos. I keep pushing it farther each time a take it out to the field nearby. So far I’ve flown it 2,600 ft or so away from my and the streaming feed stays strong, but only if you’re in an open field with a good line of sight to the drone itself, otherwise it gets a bit laggy.
It can take quite a beating too. I’ve crashed it 3 times into trees now. Only once did it need a blade/prop replacement since one got cracked. Otherwise it gets right back up, dusts itself off, laughs, then it keeps flying like nothing ever happened.
The camera modes are fun, been playing with those too. For this price point you even get a “follow target” mode. So I had my kiddo be the target and run around the field. It tracks him pretty well, as long as he doesn’t do a 180 on a dime and run the other direction and it can’t keep him in frame fast enough so it loses track…which is to be expected from any drone really.
The speed is amazing. It’s slow enough in beginner mode where you never feel like it will get away from you. Normal mode kicks it up quite a few notches to where flying it around is quick and fun, then you get to play with all of the distance and height limiters.
Now sport mode is ridiculously fast. 35mph out of this little thing is nuts.
Battery life is drained on sport mode, respectfully so. Batteries seem to last between 20-25 mins depending on use. Which is surprisingly quite longer than you’d think, especially if you’re used to $50-100 drones. Night and day difference.
My only gripe with it is that it could use some quieter propellers. It’s significantly louder than my neighbor’s DJI Mini 3.
Speaking of, these are two very similar and comparable drones. Practically all the same features, but the DJI has a slightly better camera and controller.
This one has some features that the DJI doesn’t have, and the DJI has features that the Potensic doesn’t have. However, for the price, I can nearly buy two of these at the discounted rate for the price of one DJI…and my neighbor even tells me every time we fly together that he is super impressed with this Potensic and that he nearly bought this one too before he got the DJI.
Overall, if you want the best entry drone out there with some of the best features for the best price. Look no further.

I couldn't decide whether to give 3- or 4-stars, but customer service was exceptional. The drone itself had some funky issues, but CS was super quick to reply and wanted to make everything as right as possible.
The drone itself is pretty good for its price range. A negative that I can't get over is the camera will jump angles, and only in certain directions or certain modes. The jump happening and the angle it jumps to is consistent and repeatable. CS decided it was inertia, but after testing and conversations, it is definitely a mechanical or firmware flaw. It can be worked around, but you'll have to sacrifice some things like shooting straight down while flying forward.
The other bigger negatives that I was told I can ignore is the non-stop "please calibrate" kind of message. That and calibrating it as described and shown, the horizontal works nearly 100% of the time, and the vertical calibration fails maybe 80% of the time. I've tried blue sky and cloudy days - blue skies work a little more often but isn't making a huge difference.
Compared to YouTube drone comparisons, it didn't steady itself as well as they showed. On occasion, it would get silly and circle in a 5-foot circumference before re-settling into place. Those are rare and not a deal-breaker for me, but an observation.
The signal in my semi-city area let me go about 1500 feet. I would've hoped for more, but I do have a lot of two-story houses, trees, and power lines around. I haven't flown it elsewhere to know what more it's capable of.
The drone is as expected - light weight, feels sturdy opening the legs & arms, flies as expected. It's fast when set to the proper mode, and does reasonably well fighting winds. I don't think I'd easily fly it in 20mph winds as it was bouncy with less than that, but then again, the windy days I've tried was with sporadic wind gusts. The sensors seem to work as expected. The cloudy area where I live, it takes a minute to grab enough satellites to get going.
The app has a lot of settings, some of which I haven't even tinkered with, but plenty of options. I do wish I could transfer the high-res videos through the app, but you'll need to put the SD card directly into a computer to grab it that way. It also has a handful of "special flights", like boomerang or rocket. I haven't tried them, not until i can get to a more open area, but so far those are great.
The controller is really good - it feels hefty and sturdy. I like how you can daisy chain charge it with the battery hub.
The battery and their life span is pretty good. The hub definitely makes it easier. I did have lots of battery issues - I'd fully charge it, disconnect the power for 5 seconds, the reconnect the power and they'll start charging for 15 minutes as if they depleted that quickly. CS was great at replacing the bad batteries so I'd have a good set of working batteries.
It is odd that when I return things to them, Google Maps showed their business as a house. I don't mind if a legit business is working from their home or employees are helping take on deliveries, but don't tell me and insist i'm shipping to their factory warehouse for testing when it's a residence. (Of course, google maps can be in the wrong here, too.)
I am grateful their CS did replace problematic batteries, and were so extremely communicative throughout the process.
Happy flying!

The Potensic Atom is simple to setup and get flying. It is very easy to control. The video was better than I expected. The Fly More package with the triple battery charger and case was a worthwhile option to buy. The nicely padded case that comes with the Fly More option fits everything safe and snug. Nicely done.
The attached image to this review is a screen capture from the drone of the first video I took within 5 minutes of first flying the Atom. The drone was about 15 feet away from the wife and dog and it didn't bother either of them at all, even though she was blowing the drone a raspberry. The drone is very quiet. The video is unretouched and straight from the memory card of the drone. Very nice image quality, in my humble opinion. The video output is an MP4 file format in 4K at 3480x2160 pixels and 30fps.
The remote control uses two control sticks that are screwed onto the remote when in use and unscrewed and stored on the remote control when not in use. Nice setup, but I will lose a few, I know me. So, I bought a few. They are $9 for 2 sticks. I also bought extra propeller blades at about $14 for a complete set of 8 blades (2 blades per each of 4 motors). Again, I know me, so I bought 5 extra sets. Both the controller sticks and the propeller blades are from Potensic on Amazon.
The drone also has a non-GPS flight mode using what is oddly called the Time of Flight sensor(ToF). It has a ground observing capability to fly without GPS if within 25 feet or so of the ground. This is primarily for indoor use and it works great! Scared the dog, but the drone was easily controllable indoors.
From the manual: "The ATOM is equipped with a downward vision system, it is located beneath the drone. The Downward Vision System consists of a monocular camera and a TOF module. The TOF module includes a transmitter tube and a receiver tub, it can precisely calculate the fly height above the ground by
calculating the infrared signals transmission and receiving time. In combination with the monocular camera, the system can help achieve high-precision positioning at low altitudes."
People ask about drones, "Is this drone for beginners?" The Potensic Atom is suitable for beginners due to its ease of control, and I expect other than for commercial users, the Atom will do great for most other people. The features of this drone compare favorably to any other drone I researched before I bought the Atom.
The remote controller needs a cell phone for display. I am using a 2021 Motorola g-power I had sitting in a drawer. No need to have an activated cell phone, just a phone to use as a display. A current phone that is activated works just fine too. The controller adjusts to your phone size. I did notice that Potensic seems to only offer Android and Apple iOS software for the controller. The phone must be able to connect to the Internet (I used WiFi) and download the Potensic controller app. The drone package came with USB-C and Apple Lightning connectors cables to connect the phone to the remote control. The Potesnic Pro app loaded onto the Motorola Android phone without any issues. Also, the remote controller communicates with the drone, so the phone only needs to be able to run the controller software. Meaning, the phone doesn't need to be anything special.
I am initially impressed with the drone's packaging, storage case, quality, ease of setup and use, and the quality of the video. I haven't even started to look into the various advanced capabilities of this drone, but I am looking forward to doing so. Enjoy!

This five star review is specifically for the 3 battery fly more kit, because I find it a much better value than the single battery option. For around $50 more, this kit give you two additional batteries with charging dock, a carrying case, and a 64GB name brand micro SD card. The single battery option doesn't even come with an SD card, which with storage prices right now makes the 3 battery option a great deal.
This is a great drone for beginners, offering an excellent package at a more affordable price than others. The Potensic Atom (not Atom 2) is considered to be equivalent to the DJI Mini 3 in features, and with this package I received a carrying bag that fits the controller, cables, extra propellers, screws, the drone itself, and a set of three batteries offering around 90 or so minutes of flight. Also know that this drone does not have obstacle avoidance.
If I had one complaint, it's that it seems to lose connection with the controller too easily, and this is with airplane
mode enabled on my phone to avoid interference, so you really need to keep the antennae aiming towards the drone and avoid going directly over your head.
As a beginner suitable drone, it is highly recommended to read the instructions and follow through the video guides. It is also suggested to do your research ahead of time and ensure you're following your country's laws in addition to local laws. Drone regulations can be quite strict, and this one is no exception.

Potensic went above and beyond to resolve an issue I was having with my drone. They sent a new drone in less than 24 hours after diagnosing the issue and provided prepaid postage for me to return the malfunctioning drone. This was even after the 30 days return window. This company will have your back and cares about the customer experience.
In terms of the product itself, I thought it was pretty good even when malfunctioning but having a fully functioning, unit I’m blown away with the performance. I can attest it can reach and sustain 36mph in sports mode which is on par if not better than most drones in this class. The camera quality is good and 3X zoom is achieved by lowering the resolution to 2.7K, which is almost telephoto. As mentioned before by others, it also charges the batteries in parallel, so you could in theory just continuously fly the drone with the three-pack combo, only stopping to swap batteries. It's an excellent starter drone. If you are considering this as your first drone, or haven't flown drones in years, line of sight is crucial for a reliable connection and to stay legal. It's an excellent flyer.
If I wanted any more out of this drone it would be the option to have a larger capacity battery with a built-in remote id module and maybe beacon lights for night flying to stay compliant.
The standard kit is a steal, but I guarantee you’ll be wishing you had the extra batteries in the combo package.
If you have a protective case on your phone place the phone higher on the controller so the plug is protruding and not inserted into the tuck-away, or just stick something in the tuck-away area like a piece of paper. The additional thickness of a case can cause the end that plugs into the phone to be stressed at a slight angle.

Awesome drone! Great stability even in 20+ mph winds. Great range, easy to use app. Very very user friendly. I unfortunately wrecked it, but I emailed potensic repair services (at 11pm) and they promptly replied within 20 mins!!!! Their customer service is beyond amazing! The video quality on this drone is very surprisingly clear. And surprisingly for as small and light as the drone is, it flys great. It's a mini drone with big drone attitude! both photos were taken with the potensic atom 4k 3 axis

I am really impressed with this little thing. It is really easy to setup and start flying for a noob like me, and the controls are easy to pickup and get used to. The video quality on this here is pretty impressive too, especially considering the price.
The footage is really stable, even when in `sport mode` and going pretty fast (like 20mph in winds) - and the gimbal is easy to control and get the shots that I want without thinking about it too hard.
One thing I noticed is that in `auto` mode while filming, it can really blow out highlights if there is a lot of contrast, say with green trees and white sidewalk. Fortunately you can modify the the ISO and shutter speed to help combat this, but it isn't always ideal since you only have so many flight minutes per battery. I'm hoping later firmware updates will help here, but I'm not holding my breath - and it isn't really a big deal.
Battery life is really respectable, I am impressed with how long this thing flies. In my tests its like 20 minutes before I land, but I tend to land with some battery left in case I see something else I want to film or fly over - so I don't doubt the advertised 30 minute flight time (assuming the right conditions)
The GPS is pretty good, and I quite like the autoreturn and autoland features, but I've gotten more comfortable doing both manually (its kind of fun) so I don't use that as much now. But it works, and works pretty good.
I don't have any complaints, I really like this thing and look forward to flying it when ever I see a nice day out. It checked all my boxes too:
- be a good price
- have good and stable footage
- have at least 20 minutes of flight time per charge
I didn't try any of the intelligent flight modes, and I'm not really super interested in them - but if I do try them I'll update this review with additional information on what I think about them.
But overall: this is a great drone, I love it and would buy another in a heartbeat.

Potensic have hit it out of the park for this drone.
In the sub 250g class and having 4k with a gimbal, this is an amazing drone and takes the focus away from DJI, whom have been steadily increasing their prices to beyond affordable.
Potensic does have its downsides like all budget options, the auto white balance is not good. Put it on manual and adjust on the fly to suit the scene.
The camera is true 4k, the caveat being to get 4k usable footage you need to copy directly from the sd card in a phone or pc with an sd slot. No option for a usb connection to pc. If you copy from drone to phone/pc it will only be 720p.
Performance wise. This drone really is all it’s made out to be. There’s a voucher at the minute for £30 off. It handles fairly windy days well, it’s very stable footage is great and the smoothness of the gimbal when rotating it or yawing the drone is great. No jerky movements.
No tested battery time yet as I’ve only had three 5 minute flights.
You need to provide an sd card. Amazon have a 3 pack of 32gb for £11.
I will be getting the extra battery pack with the triple charger.
The footage uploaded here is 720p as it’s downloaded to my phone. It’s no indication of the 4k quality. It does show how stable it is in a mildly windy flight.

Creo que ha sido la mejor compra del año. Un dron económico, ideal para un principiante, pero con todas las características que podrías esperar de estas pequeñas joyas de ingeniería y electrónica, comparable -y en muchos aspectos mejor- a los afamados y carísimos DJI.
El seguro a todo riesgo es también más económico que el de un DJI.
Llevo probándolo cuatro meses y no puedo estar más satisfecho con este Potensic Atom. El dron está muy bien acabado, tiene calidad y acabados inmejorables. Veo que el fabricante escucha a los usuarios en sus canales de RRSS y me sorprende ver cómo incorporan las mejoras en el firmware y la aplicación que los usuarios piden: zoom digital, mejoras en estabilización del horizonte -en el modelo que no lleva gimbal de 3 ejes-, mejoras en el uso manual de los parámetros de exposición de la cámara,...
El dron es una pequeña bestia. Vuela rapidísimo en modo "sport", la cinemática es muy buena en modo "grabación", soporta vientos relativamente fuertes -probado a 20km/h- y, comprobado en campo, mantiene el enlace estable donde otros DJI de su gama activan el RTH por pérdida de señal. La cámara estabilizada en 3 ejes graba imágenes sorprendentes en 4K y perfectamente estabilizadas. Flaquea en grabación nocturna en modo automático, mejorando algo ajustando la exposición en modo manual.
Dispone de los modos de vuelo automático habituales: cohete, espiral, boomerang,...etc muy configurables y sencillos de usar desde la aplicación. El seguimiento lo hace por análisis de imagen, no por posicionamiento GPS del mando como en otros drones económicos -o el propio Atom SE, la versión económica del 3-ejes-.
Las baterías son potentes y ligeras, de momento no han dado señales de flaqueza. Recomiendo el kit "vuela más" con bolsa de transporte, tres baterías y triple cargador, porque es mucho más versátil.
En resumen, se trata de un dron económico con aspiraciones a ponérselo difícil a DJI y su actual abuso de mercado en esta gama de productos (hasta 250 gramos), con precios mucho más razonables y funcionalidad similar o mejor.
Como aspecto a mejorar se echa en falta una mayor disponibilidad de repuestos, aunque de momento la maca está respondiendo satisfactoriamente -en redes sociales se leen muchos comentarios en este sentido- reemplazando drones completos en caso de accidente a precios reducidos. La marca ya ha indicado que está trabajando en ello.
Me surpreendi com imagem, bem mais do que eu esperava. Vale a pena!

Definitely yearning for more now, yet those "nice" days are becoming far-n-few between so hopefully we don't have to wait too long.
Right now as of my review the Potensic Atom is discounted with an additional coupon that can be applied. Very good price in my opinion for something of this caliber. Also included in the package, for a limited time, is a 64GB Lexar MicroSD card. So other than providing a smartphone for the RC everything else is there to start flying A.S.A.P.

This is my second Veeniix UAS (drone). As a gift, my wife purchased the V11PRO that used a your cell phone as the screen and photo/video capture. That unit worked great but was inconvenient since I use a quality case on my phone, I had to remove the phone case every time I wanted to fly. I’m normally not a review kinda guy but I would of given the V11PRO 3 or 4 star if I rated it because of the phone inconvenience.
As far as I can tell the UAS is the same as the original V11PRO. Same quality gimble mount 4k camera and same quality construction. Flying the unit is simple and easy. The users manual is on the RC and easy to go through. The RC screen is about the size of the large phones on the market. The screen is sharp with good color and contrast so it’s easy to see in bright sun light. It’s touch screen so it’s easy to navigate through the various menus and settings. It fits good in my hands and all of the buttons and controls are within easy reach.
As you can see from the photo’s, the carry case is different and I like it better. It’s not bigger or smaller but I think the soft case is easier to pack. There are spare props, charging cables, spare control sticks, 2 batteries, and a bag for the RC so you don’t scratch the screen. You need to supply the micro SD cards (32G-256G), one for the UAS and one for the RC. You’ll also need to supply a good quality charger.
The easiest way to pull the photos and video off the UAS is to have the Veeniix App and download them to your phone. This works over wifi and once I figured out the procedure, it was easy. It doesn’t appear you can just get them off the SD card. I tried and it seemed like I either lost files or there was nothing. Might need to play with that more and I admit I didn’t take a lot of time to read everything.
I’ve flown this unit for about an hour and half so far and everything is working as advertised. I’ve also attached a few photo’s and a video for reference. It’s done everything as advertised and I’ve no issues in my test flights. Time will tell but I’m going to give 5 stars. Did I mention how much I liked the new RC2 with the built in screen?

Overall, I'm very pleased with this drone. Especially the quality of the photos and videos. It is very stable in flight and hover adding to the media quality. Operation is pretty straight forward. The auto return is your friend and is a safety feature you will come to appreciate. My experience is flight time and battery duration is not as long as stated but part of that could be due to flying conditions such as head wind, etc. Once you are familiar with operation it could be a little faster but generally the speed is sufficient. My reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is loss of signal that reduces range that results in auto return before mission completion. In my case I believe that this is due to the geographic area I mainly operate in which is heavily wooded with very tall trees making line of site between the drone and the controller difficult. I have overcome this to some extent by using the map feature and flying way-points which seems to allow the drone to operate autonomously. Overall a really good drone for the price point.

You don't need to spend a ton of money to get a great drone that works perfectly. In my experience, Veeniix is the best choice. Their products are awesome, and their promise to treat customers well is much better than most other companies.

I would like to start out by saying I also have the older V11 Gim2 drone from Veenix. When I heard they had a new V11 pro, I couldn't wait to try it. The new V11 pro is the left drone in pictures. The drone comes in a very nice case. Comes with the necessary adapters needed for charging the batteries and connecting any phone to the remote, android or iOS. The in-app step-by-step instructions makes it super easy for beginners to start flying. Compared to the older V11, you do seem to get better quality pictures and a longer battery life. I did fly my old and new one back to back to see. The motors in the drone must be more efficient as the batteries are actually the same capacity (3500mah), and will actually interchange with the older V11. So if you also have the older version like me, you will be able to use the batteries. The max range does seem to be inflated from a lot of the drone mfg. I was able to get a distance of 2500ft away according to the remote, but was having the remote saying weak signal with the FPV being hit or miss. Other than that, it flew very well. Just like the older V11, it makes me feel confident that I will always be able to bring it back safely. It never seems to fly out of control, even in higher winds. It also has a lot of the nice features carry over from the older V11 like the detachable joysticks that snap into the bottom of the remote and USB cable that connects directly to the remote that helps keep your phone charged during use. All the in-app features also seem to work well like follow me, waypoint etc. Overall, it seems like a great drone in this price range that I would recommend to anyone looking for one.

I rarely write reviews, even when a product performs well, which I admit is probably my own laziness. However, I feel compelled to leave a review for this product because of how thoroughly disappointed I am with it.
I genuinely wish DJI were still an option, because this drone is nothing more than an expensive paperweight. I consider myself an experienced drone flyer. I have owned several drones over the years, and while I’m certainly not a professional cinematography pilot, I know what I’m doing. Unfortunately, this drone behaves as if it has a mind of its own.
On multiple occasions, it has randomly initiated a return-to-home and landing sequence without warning. When this happens, attempting to cancel the action or manually take control is useless—the drone ignores inputs, lands where it shouldn’t, or crashes into nearby objects. This has happened repeatedly.
The battery performance is even worse. Each battery is fully charged before flight, yet I’m lucky to get seven minutes of flight time per battery. This isn’t a defective battery issue—I experienced the same problem with all three batteries, including an additional one I purchased hoping it would solve the issue. It didn’t.
Despite very limited use, the drone has extremely low total flight time because it simply isn’t enjoyable or reliable to fly. At best, I might get 21 minutes total across all three batteries. Once the battery reaches around 50%, it suddenly drops to 25%, triggers an automatic return, and once again refuses to allow manual override. The drone then lands wherever it decides, regardless of surroundings.
Yes, you get what you pay for, and this is clearly a budget drone—but even a lower-priced product should be functional and enjoyable. This is neither. Flying it is stressful, frustrating, and ultimately pointless. The only one time I had fun flying this thing is the day I opened it. After that nothing but, buyers remorse. Would give 0 stars if possible!
My advice: save your money. Buy a good used DJI drone, or if they become available again in the U.S., purchase one new. The higher price is absolutely worth it for reliability, flight time, and actual enjoyment. If you are still within the return window for this drone, return it immediately. It is not worth the headache.

review_title: Amazing, professional drone results compared to hobby drones
review_body:
Technology advances fast. Just five years ago this would have been a $1500 professional grade drone. To think you can get pro-quality performance, excellent stability in light to moderate breeze, stunning images, and good flight time for under $300 is surprising. The image is from my first flight with zero training and default settings. Videos are smooth and crisp.

Unboxing though initial setup is frankly daunting, but the in-app walkthrough is clear and unhurried and I went from inatalling the DJI Fly app to flying in under 20 minutes. Flight controls are legendary. The Cine setting is solid stability like a vintage Rolls Royce, while Sport mode is an exciting FPS experience that was just outside my comfort zone with my limited experience but I never felt out of control and frantic the way inexpensive hobby drones do. I haven't ended scratched the surface of the settings menu, but for what I need for Youtube content creation and scenic b-roll this works perfectly. It's also compact enough to slip into my hydration pack for capturing my motorcycle rides. I wish I'd bought this sooner!

One note about the connector cables for iPhone users! If your phone is in a heavy duty case, it will still fit in the phone holder, but the connector may not seat properly due to the small lip molded into the connection cable. No problem, a Lighting extender adapter works just fine.

review_title: Fun beginner drone, but I wish I had bought the version with longer flight time
review_body:
I bought this drone as a beginner and had a lot of fun flying it. Setup was straightforward, the controls were easy to learn, and it was stable enough for casual flying around the yard and local park. The drone feels lightweight but reasonably durable, and I was able to get it in the air within minutes of unboxing.

The camera quality is decent for the price and good enough for capturing some fun aerial shots and videos. The app connection worked without major issues, and features like altitude hold made it easier to control than I expected.

My biggest complaint is the battery life. The advertised flight time may be achievable under ideal conditions, but in real-world use it felt fairly short. Just when I was getting comfortable and enjoying the flight, it seemed like it was already time to bring the drone back and recharge.

Looking back, I probably should have purchased the version that comes with additional batteries or extended flight time. Having extra flying time would have made the experience much more enjoyable and reduced the amount of waiting between flights.

Overall, this is a good entry-level drone that is easy to fly and fun to use. If you're considering it, I would strongly recommend getting the package with extra batteries or longer flight time if it's available. You'll likely appreciate the added flying time much more than I did after the fact.

review_body:
I been flying drones since Dji phantom 2. I've had quite a few. My personal best was a toss up between the phantom 4 pro vs. Air2s (air 2s new so I give that the winner). So I've had my fair share with different cameras. I currently own even the neo which is a pretty damn good drone with the remote. But none the less, if you want a cheap decent camera with a couple basic features then I 100% point you to this drone the mini 4k.

You can produce some amazing footage with this drone if you know a little about camera settings via ISO, Shutter etc. but what really makes the footage cinematic and looking really amazing is ND filters.

Look at my video, I just went to my local waterfront and flew around sunset time with I believe a 8ND filter. Or possibly 16ND filter. I forgot lol

But I've had three of these mini 4k drones. Only cause in comparison to dji other drones, this is only 200 dollars so I keep buying it lol. My first one I bought I attached floaters to the bottom so I can land and take off on water (I like to fish and trying to land on a rocky boat is difficult in tight area so landing on water sounded easier lol) but the product I bought blocked the sensors and when I flew up like 50 ft the sensors being blocked tricked it to think it was near ground level and iust initiated automatic landing feature 😂😂😂 plopped out the sky and broke. 2nd drone I was out in the woods of PA camping and I saw a body of water like half a mile away, so I got overly confident and flew my drone out of line of sight, and lost connection. Didn't program my Return to Home flight feature since I didn't think anything was gonna happen so I lost it lolol.

Both my fault so this third time 😂😂😂 I'ma treat it like an expensive drone and really stop pushing my luck and my Amazon credit.

Drone is less than 250g so I don't even gotta register it. I just take the "trust" drone Test online for free and I'm good to fly recreationally within the realm of state, local and FAA law.

This is a beautiful drone. I didn’t think the tiny gimbal would be as good as it is and have the range of motion that it does. You can look straight ahead or adjust up to 90 degrees for straight down. The props aren’t visible in the camera no matter have fast you go. The image quality is excellent and it does seem to do some extra processing if you capture images into your phone vs the onboard memory as seen in the attached photos.
I have yet to figure out when it goes to the phone and when it only goes to the drone. It seems that if I use the phone touchscreen to take a photo it goes to the phone and using the controller shutter it goes only to the drone (for more rapid shooting with less overhead).
The controls are dead simple and it seems pretty hard to mess up this drone. I wouldn’t call myself a beginner, but I think even if you are new it shouldn’t be too bad compared to drones or the past that had much fewer guardrails. I love how all the usual drone controls work like moving the sticks apart and down to turn the props on. The drone itself is quite delicate so it’s not for the faint of heart or brutes expecting industrial durability. It doesn’t go above 120m by default which seems severely limiting but a good guard for new flyers I suppose.
I can’t figure out a good way to charge the drone while transferring photos and videos from it since it needs to be on for that but when you turn it on it wants to set up for flight and flashes amber as it finds issues with the gimbal and the arms being folded. It does not seem to like this and I don’t think it’s good to leave it in this state but what am I to do? Yes I can take out the memory card and read the media that way, which is something I’ll probably start to do. It is much handier, however, just opening the app with controller attached and picking the media, transfer, and it’s done. I like to be selective, though, and only pick the ones that I want, which means browsing all the media. The drone flashing errors while I do this doesn’t seem optimal and I haven’t found a workaround yet. Overall, this is a wonderful drone at $299 CAD.

I took the drone out for a test flight right after receiving it. It flies extremely steadily, the gimbal delivers excellent anti-shake performance, and aerial footage is crisp. It’s easy to learn to operate. One-touch takeoff/landing and intelligent follow mode work wonderfully. It’s a fantastic aerial photography companion for travels, and I’m totally satisfied!
The drone is lightweight and portable, with stable image transmission signals and battery life meeting expectations. Obstacle avoidance brings great peace of mind, making it beginner-friendly. Capture scenery from a bird’s-eye view — well worth buying!
Exquisite craftsmanship with a foldable design that saves storage space. Aerial image quality exceeds expectations. Time-lapse and one-touch short video functions are highly practical. Customer service staff offer patient explanations. Recommended for aerial photography enthusiasts!

review_title: Perfect Beginner Drone, Easy to Fly and So Much Fun!
review_body:
I bought this drone on a whim because I wanted a simple way to capture some aerial photos and videos while traveling, and I am impressed.

First, setup was quick and easy. Within minutes I had it in the air. The one-button takeoff and landing feature takes away a lot of the intimidation factor if you’ve never flown a drone before. The altitude hold feature kept it surprisingly stable, which made getting photos and videos much easier than I expected.

The camera quality is great for the price. I was able to capture beautiful overhead views that I never would have gotten with my phone alone. Being able to see the live image on my phone while flying made the experience even more enjoyable.

I also appreciate how compact and lightweight it is. It folds up small enough to toss into a travel bag without taking up much space. The two included batteries were a nice bonus and gave me plenty of flight time.

For anyone looking for an affordable, beginner-friendly drone that is fun to fly and produces impressive photos and videos, this is an excellent choice. It exceeded my expectations and has already become one of my favorite travel gadgets.

Highly recommend! 🚁✨📸

P.S. If you’re nervous about flying a drone for the first time, don’t be. This one is incredibly user-friendly and a great way to learn.

review_title: A Fantanstic X69 Drone to Purchase!
review_body:
This model X69 drone is a great drone for anyone who may be interested in learning to fly a drone for the first time. With the features it has to offer and an affordable price, it makes for an easy experience and fun flight time.
It comes in a nice case that has everything you need including a clear to follow user manual, 2 batteries and a controller that after charging it up, you’re able to be up and flying right out of the case. With its one takeoff press button you’re immediately up in the air and in flight mode. The controller has a nice holder built-in for your smartphone that after installing the app, you’re able to see your flight time on the screen and a whole lot more.

Set up is a breeze and self explanatory. Charge up the batteries, which by the way, have good life. They give you a good amount of time to enjoy your drone. It has an app you can use if you want to control it while viewing the camera, and my iPhone 13 fit well in the telescopic controller. review_body: I was pleasantly surprised by this drone! The camera quality is clear and sharp for both pictures and videos. The instructions were very clear and easy to follow. The app was also easy to use and get the hang of quickly. It took me a minute to figure out the controls for flying, but I was comfortable after just a few minutes! review_body:
This is a fun drone for the money. It's a good first drone, but not a great drone overall.

I bought this drone to see if I would even enjoy flying a drone and it turns out I really enjoyed flying this one. It's a challenge to fly, and for the price, I wasn't too worried about crashing it. And, I've crashed it a LOT. I'm impressed that it still flies, actually. It pretty tough, though I think it's starting to show signs of wear.
It's not easy to fly, but it's great for training. There's no obstacle avoidance or station keeping, you have to pay attention to what you are doing and learn how to control this little drone.
It's maneuverable and fun to fly, but gets a bit hard to control when coming in for a landing.

The battery seems to last for a while, and having two of them is great. The controller works well and is easy to use. I even like the little soft case it comes with.
The drone folds up small and is easy to set up.

Setup was pretty easy on my iphone. Download the app and connect to the drone wifi, and you can see through the camera. You don't even need the camera to fly, you can skip that part if you're not taking photos/videos or interested in POV flying.
The connection is laggy, which makes POV flying harder. The connection also starts to drop with much distance. I'd guess the video feed drops out around 20 yards, though the controls still work.

The bad part is the camera. It is not good at all.
Video is shaky and shows lots of artifacts. The photos remind me of my first cell phone. I thought this drone might be fun to try a little drone photography with, but the quality is no good at all.
It's also hard to frame photos, as there is no station-keeping .
If you want a drone for photography, this isn't it. I wasn't expecting a great camera, but not this bad.

This is a fun toy, but not a serious drone.
I enjoyed flying this one so much, I brought a better one. I still fly this one though, for practice and because I'm not affraid to crash it.

review_body: I am thrilled with this drone! Unpacking and start-up is a breeze, and it took no time to put it into action. Included are all the accessories needed for years of use, including extra blades, charging cable, 2 batteries, etc. I really like the size and look of this drone and it's easy to control with my android phone. The camera provides for very high quality pictures and video. When using this for just fun it is very capable, and the flip function is very nice. The drone had no issues with basic location options, such as headless mode and gravity control. One thing that really stands out with this model is the 3-speed option, something I have not seen in other comparable drones. I'd recommend this drone for teenagers and adults, but it could be controlled by a younger child with some supervision. I highly recommend buying this drone, especially with the affordable price.

This drone is ready to fly out of the box, very good quality, easy to use with a lot of functionality for a very good price.
It stays up in the air for 35 to 40 minutes on 1 battery and you get 2 with it, I bough another one for almost nothing, it gives me at least 1h 30 of flying.
