If you are looking for a reliable, easy to fly with quite some functionality and on top an awesome customer service, for a good price, you have to look into it.

I was skeptical about its stability in the wind, but tests shows it handles surprisingly well for its size. Not hard to operate, but I have to go through the operating manual to learn what more cool things I can do with this drone. I cannot wait to take this drone out next time I go outdoor target shooting again and capture some cool pics and videos.
The Intelligent Flight Modes, particularly like follow-me work surprisingly well for a budget drone. I hope I'm not sharing my opinion too soon, but I'm loving this drone so far! Had to reach out to their customer service too for minor issues and questions, and they're very helpful.

THIS IS A GREAT BUY!!!
It's been great for taking photos of my and my friend's properties. The picture is crystal clear, and the connection to the phone being hardwired makes it seamless. UPDATE: The drone is still working excellently. I have had it for about 8 to 9 months. The only issue I've had is that it was left out for about five days in torrential rainstorms. It did have the battery in the drone at the time.Although it was in its case with the top wide open, I put the drone and the remote control on top of one of my floor heat vents. After a couple of days, I put the battery back into the drone, turned it on, and it fired up with no issue. Unfortunately, although the blue light below the right stick on the controller lit when I tried to charge it, it did not turn back on. I reached out to the manufacturer and within four hours received a response from them. They are sending me a new controller free of charge.
This company has been amazing to deal with. The drone itself takes amazing photographs. As I own a construction company, it has taken quite a few pictures of shingles, and the definition is clear between tabs, showing their contrast. I've also gotten it stuck a hundred yards up in a tree and crashed it quite a few times, including inside my home, even though that was a bad idea from the start. If you're looking for a fun drone that's easy to fly, this definitely gets it done. If you're looking to take photographs for your business, this thing is great.

This was a Christmas gift for my boyfriend. Wow. What a great drone. Once you get comfortable with the drone and controls this thing is a blast. I was a bit skeptical at first but was immediately impressed. We took it hiking and was able to get some great quality pictures. I am also a flooring contractor and I am able to get some overhead pictures and videos. Simple set from the beginner to the pro. Video and picture quality is exceptional. Even with a good windy breezy day this drone stays pretty stable. For the price this drone has it all. You do have to register the drone with the FAA. The manual and website makes the process simple. $5. Blah blah blah.. the best part.... are you sitting down?? One day there was some interference and the drone went rogue and landed on a roof on an adjacent building. E0 foot ladder and retrieval of 5 pieces I thought I was done. I contacted GLEESFUN and told them the details. I sent them the info they requested and..................they replaced the drone. I know right ?? AWESOME!!! great company. Fun drone.

This Drone is GREAT!!! Strong performance at a cost that outclasses many higher priced drones. The controls are smooth, the signal stays reliable, and the camera quality is clear for everyday flying. The build feels solid and the battery life is consistent. If you want real value for your money this is a dependable option that competes with models that cost much more. I would buy it again without hesitation. My only wish is that it could avoid the trees in my state but that is on me not the drone.
I had a few questions for customer service and they were fast to respond and assist.

After my test flight today I must say I find this drone is pretty impressive. I can't speak about range yet since my property is in a subdivision and close to a transmission tower so interference is an issue, but so far I can say this drone handles very well as far as flight characteristics. The build quality is solid and appears very durable. The headlights make a really cool addition. It also has an internal Remote ID transponder for FAA compliance. This is no toy drone. This is a serious aerial photography tool for the money.
Concerning the camera, photos and videos are eye poppingly sharp and detailed but the camera does have some limits. Thin objects like an antenna tower and tree branches loose detail when set before a bright sky (sun not actually in the background but its brightness is). Darker areas lose a bit of detail and appear a tad grainy while the drone is in motion. These are not complaints, just honest observations. I'm not expecting perfection from an 1/3.2 inch CMOS. I am impressed with the image quality overall. As for the stability of the videos, I am REALLY impressed. The breeze was buffeting the drone a bit but the live video feed and recorded video doesn't show it at all. I'd say it's just as good as EIS. This is one amazing gimbal system.
Overall I'm very happy with this drone and hope to take it to some more scenic areas some time during the Spring away from the RF interference I have here. I kept it over my property at the beginner's altitude and didn't test the range. From experience I can say it wouldn't be all that good considering the WIFI congestion in my neighborhood. I'll post an update including photos and video in the future.
To finish up, this is a quality drone that in my opinion is well worth the price, offering durability and functionality rivaling, and actually surpassing, a more expensive drone I purchased and returned do to sub par performance for its price. I definitely recommend it.

This was a tough purchase for me at first because I already own a Sky Rover X1, which is basically a Mini 4 Pro clone, and I’m very happy with it. But the Mini 5 Pro is on a different level. DJI builds a more polished product. The camera is better, the sensors are better, the obstacle avoidance is better, and the whole system just feels more refined.
I’ve only flown it a few times, thanks to the Pacific Northwest weather, but every flight has been smooth and impressive. It does everything my X1 can do, but with better image quality and more capability overall. The Fly More Combo is absolutely worth it. The three batteries last a long time. While DJI advertises 54 minutes, I was comfortably getting around 45 to maybe 50 minutes.
One thing to keep in mind: this drone sits right at the 250-gram limit. If you add anything to it, you’ll go over. Because of that, I picked up a Remote ID module so I stay compliant. It’s not a downside to the drone itself, just something worth noting for anyone who plans to add accessories.
The RC-2 controller is another highlight. You don’t have to hook up your phone or a tablet, and the built-in display is excellent. It makes setup faster and cleaner. The controller is a little heavy, though, so I recommend getting a lanyard. On longer flights, you can really feel it in your arms.
Overall, this combo is outstanding, and I’m glad I got it when I did.
Pros:
Excellent build quality and very polished
Noticeably better camera quality
Great obstacle avoidance and lighting
Smooth, stable flying even in mixed conditions
Fly More Combo gives you three long-lasting batteries.
RC-2 controller has a bright, built-in screen so no phone is needed
The lanyard option helps with controller weight.
Very quiet for its size
Cons:
Adding any accessory pushes it over 250 grams, which means Remote ID
Controller is a bit heavy without a lanyard
Battery life is a little under the advertised 54 minutes, but still strong
Summary:
An excellent drone with great performance, long battery life, a fantastic controller, and very polished features. I highly recommend it.

A pretty pricey drone but very good drone that makes up for it. The images turn out beautiful after editing. The extra registering for the extra weight when using the extended flight batteries is definitely worth it, as this kit provides enough battery to not worry about battery anymore. I have not rs. into problems of this thing getting affected by winds a lot, so i think the wind resistance for normal use is fine. The med-tele ability is good for people who don’t need to zoom in a lot but just maybe sometimes get a closer view of the subject. The drones pretty portable as you can just stuff all the stuff into the shoulder bag and just go. Some downsides, are that it doesn’t have adjustable aperture and putting on ND filters is a pain. And in special terrain the signal can be lost almost immediately, when i was in the mountains. The screen of the RC-2 is very good, and using it is similar as using a phone but without the hassle of attaching a phone on it. Worth buying it for people who are into drone imaging but not that beginner since a crash can cost 1.2K.

Excellent drone and it arrived working as it should. Only downside is for U.S customers like me, the DJI Care refresh (the coverage insurance you could buy directly from DJI) isn’t available in our region; due to ongoing geopolitical issues with DJI’s parent company. However, this is the best drone for quality and size. Highly recommend if you are a person who likes to travel and wants to document your trips in a fuller way. Use the DJI simulator and practice flying you need a few hours of practice before becoming confident. Use YouTube as your learning space to watch videos explaining the drone and its settings. Use the quick shots features they are amazing for beginners to get beautiful drone footage. The controls are very easy to follow. Battery life is around its quoted time of 45minutes to 51 minutes. It’s a high quality portable drone that can be wrapped up and fit in your small backpack. Get the combo plus fly more bundle it’s worth the extra money.

I purchased the DJI Mini 5 Pro from Amazon and the delivery itself was smooth with no issues. However, things started to go wrong as soon as I opened the box. The packaging looked like it had been resealed, I didn’t see the usual green tab, which made me question whether the unit was truly new.
When I tried charging the batteries, the charging hub behaved oddly. One battery just sat there blinking and wouldn’t charge properly. I had to switch slots multiple times before I finally got all of them to charge. The controller, at least, charged without any issues.
Next came the firmware updates, and that’s where things completely fell apart. The controller took an unusually long time to download the update. When I started updating the drone, it failed at 70% with an error saying the battery was below 20% — even though the battery showed a single LED and, after reinserting it, turned out to be fully charged. I tried again with a different battery, and it failed at 93%. Same issue with the third battery.
I then connected the controller to DJI Assistant 2 and managed to update the controller successfully. But when updating the drone through the software, it repeatedly failed again around 92–93%. I also received a “firmware mismatch” error. I tried multiple cables, rebooted my PC, and repeated the process several times with no success.
At that point, I gave up and initiated a return. What made the situation worse was that Amazon did not offer a replacement option during the return process, something they used to do. Instead, I had to place a completely new order and spend another $1,230 upfront while waiting for the refund.
The replacement order created even more issues. Delivery was pushed to two days, and a signature was required, which didn’t work with my schedule. I ended up canceling that order and buying the same drone locally instead. Within 20 minutes, it was ready for pickup, and that unit worked perfectly. Firmware updated on the first try, and it flew without any problems.
In total, I had to temporarily spend over $2,400 just to end up with a working product. That’s not acceptable. Amazon should have offered a direct replacement without requiring me to front that kind of money again.
I returned the defective drone within 14 hours of receiving it.
Final verdict: The drone itself is great when it works, but this unit was likely defective (or possibly previously opened/returned), and the return/replacement process through Amazon was disappointing. Giving 1 star — half for the defective product, and half for how the situation was handled.

I am a first time drone user and my interest is primarily photography and videography.
I have eyed the DJI Mini series for a couple of years as a first foray into Ariel photography and videography.
The upgrades that DJI instituted in the latest version including comprehensive obstacle avoidance and the 1” sensor made me commit to buying one.
As seen from the posted photograph, this is a small drone.
Before it was delivered I used the flight simulator that DJI has in its store app on the iPad.
This helped me gain experience before I even received the drone.
I chose the fly more combo plus with the bigger batteries because with the regular batteries the drone is specified to weigh 249.9 g, which is under the limit to register it. But considering that there is just 0.1g under regulation, tiny variations in production would put it over the top anyway.
The drone with the larger batteries weigh 294g. I registered it with the FAA and took the TRUST test too.
The FAA had this model in their registration process even though DJI can’t sell it directly in the US.
The activation process was an issue primarily because DJI WIFI will not work with secure home networks. So, instead of making my home network insecure by opening it up, I chose to activate it through my cell phone,
That is the only issue I have with DJI drones. I wish they would fix it.
DJI on the other hand has comprehensive information on how to use this drone via it DJI store app.
The RC2 remote with its built in screen and fly more app is superb. It is really well engineered with superb software that lets you know about flying restrictions.
It also can search areas that you want to go to and the regulations there. There’s also reviews by other drone flyers on that location.
My first flight was really easy because of time spent on the simulator.
I did an auto takeoff from the DJI bag and then manually landed primarily because the drone had some issues auto landing on the small DJI bag that came with the drone. This was entirely my fault because I forgot to get the landing pad I purchased separately.
The photographs and videos of the pacific coast were superb and exceeded my expectations.
This drone comes highly recommended, even though at this moment it’s not covered by DJI’s warranty due to ongoing issues with selling directly here.
The only negative is connecting via WiFi is a big issue. I have however been able to use my iPhones cellular connection to activate and upgrade the firmware. However I have not been able to download maps by cellular as yet.
Still comes highly recommended for both the capabilities of the drone and DJI’s comprehensive support system for its users.

Took time given import delays. The seller was patient and responded to communication through the process. I operate enterprise drones as part of my duties and wanted to replace an older personal airframe. The specific aircraft I received was able to register with the FAA.
The M5P is fantastic and handles well in flight. Easy to fly as is the norm with DJI. A little touchy at times compared to larger enterprise drones.
Video and photo quality is superb and the built-in enhanced tracking/follow features are great. You can count and check cows with it.
I purchased the fly more plus bundle, which does activate RID for those of you who fly under Part 107. Weight variance does exist in this model, even with the standard battery which will require registration if over 250g.
Flight time, everyone wants the full advertised time but that is never realistic unless you’re flying indoors with no negative effects to the drone like low temps. I’ve got about 35 minutes on a single battery, but this is also playing it conservatively on energy levels.
Size of your hand folded up and the cases sold for this model are great. I highly recommend getting a hard case in lieu of the soft bag DJI ships with this. All packed up, it can go anywhere.
Landing gear: Definitely have a landing pad or an elevated gear attachment as it sits low on the deck. Any height of grass will get into the props and I’d be weary landing on gravel. The hood of a car works in a pinch.

I've had the Phantom 4 Pro, Mavic Pro, Mavic 2 Pro, Mavic 3 Classic, and now the Mini 5 Pro (And I flew Walkera drones before DJI was a thing). I sold the 3 classic earlier this year and have been on the fence for a while regarding the mini 5 pro. The biggest deterrent for me was its wind performance as I like to fly in pre/post-stormy weather occasionally. So knowing this drone wouldn't hold hold up to larger drones in that aspect, the rest looked promising.
First impressions? Pretty blown away. I got the fly more plus cimbo. The video feed to the controller is noticeably better than the Mavic 3 classic or any predecessor. So smooth. The transmission is stronger too. I can fly lower farther, also with noticeably less interference. The speed isnt as fast in sport mode ad me Mavic classic drones but the mini 5 pro is no slouch. For all practical purposes it does the job. It does draw more bird attention than the slightly larger drones which is worth mentioning. I can still outrun them through! The mini 5 pro powers up when you open the legs and powers off when you close them. I thought that was a nice touch. It has the option to override that if you don't want it to power itself up and down on its own. Saves time though and keeps it simple. The vertical shooting and zoom features will get used a lot for sure. The zoom is more impressive than I was expecting, and while not perfect, is smooth and more than useful. I saw a lot of reviews saying this drone is whisper quiet. I don't believe that to be the case. It's maybe slightly quieter than the Mavic series. If you bust out the dB meter you'll probably see a difference but as far as my ears, I can still hear this drone a fair way away. That's no deal breaker but worth noting. It's very light in your hand and hand launching/landing is a breeze. The plus batteries get you close to an hour of flight time which is amazing. I won't need to winder if I need to bring a charger with me. Maybe for the controller if anything. There is no cover for the micro sd card slot, which is nice when loading/offloading your card, but also makes me hesitant to fly it in fog/clouds. If you install the DJI fly app on your phone you can transfer files wirelessly for social media and things like that.
If I had to find a negative about this mini 5 pro? Probably the wind performance, but there has to be a sacrifice somewhere. The amount of time thats an issue for me compared to the ease of transport, deployment, extended battery life, makes the trade off worth it for me. Watch out for big birds and wind. Other than that it's perfect. DJI needs to be careful with the mini 6 pro or they'll for sure cannabalaize their mavic line. Not complaining.
TLDR: If I had a Mavic 2 Pro, Mavic 3 Classic, or Mini 5 Pro offered to me for $1k each I'd take the Mini 5 Pro.
Great drone for the price. This is the best mini drone on the market.

From the box to the skies in minutes! With no previous drone piloting experience, this turned out to be a fun and intuitive experience for us. Setup was a breeze... fully charge the batteries and controller, remove the drone, deploy the collapsible propeller arms, set it on a flat surface, hold down the power button until the drone comes alive with beeps and flashing lights, power up the controller, and wait for the drone to establish a connection with the controller. Press the lift-off button - you'll hear an "all clear" warning and the blades begin rotation; press it again, and the drone leaps into the air! Initially, we started with very subtle, gentle commands to orient ourselves with the control sensitivity... up, down, rotate direction, forward/reverse, and left and right. As new pilots, we did have a few unexpected entanglements with our trees and some plants... however, even with a few tumbles, the sturdy design, as well as the flexible and non-rigid prop connections, did just fine and were not damaged. Our drone was airborne for a good 20 minutes while we worked out our new flying skills without any noticeable dip in available battery power. We managed to record a few minutes of one of our flights and the resolution and color were way beyond our expectations. Next, we want to explore more of the included features... this little drone packs a punch with advanced features and is easy enough for a complete novice to use.

review_title: Contixo F33 Drone – Excellent Flight Time and Outstanding Customer Support
review_body:
I have a lot of drones—most of them are small FPV drones, but I also own a few larger camera drones. This one has become my number two favorite. My number one is still my DJI Mini 4K, mainly because the video quality is just better. Both shoot 4K, but you can tell DJI is a camera company at heart.

Where the Contixo F33 really shines is flight time. My Mini 4K starts giving me range anxiety after about 20–25 minutes, even with multiple batteries. The F33, on the other hand, can stay up much longer, which makes it the drone I reach for when I want a longer, more relaxed flight session.

The camera quality is still good—definitely better than most of the other 4K drones I own—it’s just not quite on the same level as DJI. Still, for general aerial video and photos it performs very well.

I did have a small issue early on while flying at my in-laws’ house where the drone completely lost signal, and I had to go retrieve it. I opened a support ticket with Contixo, and a few days later they contacted me and had me send the drone back for inspection. They ended up sending me an entire replacement drone, which I was very impressed by.

Even more surprising, I had accidentally left my Samsung 256GB microSD card in the drone I returned. The support rep actually reached out to tell me she found the card and mailed it back to me, which was honestly above and beyond. You don’t see customer service like that very often anymore. They even included spare propellers with the replacement.

Since receiving the replacement drone, the range has been excellent and I haven’t had any further issues. It’s also fairly quick—around 23 mph, which is plenty for a camera drone. Obviously it’s not something you’d race, but it moves along nicely.

The obstacle avoidance works well too, which is reassuring when those tree branches seem to come out of nowhere. It does a good job warning you and preventing accidents.

Overall, I’m very impressed with both the drone and the company. The flight time is fantastic, performance is solid, and their customer service was genuinely outstanding. Hats off to Ria and the team.

review_title: The first one of its kind
review_body:
This claw is the first one of its kind that I have found!
I want to start out by saying the build of the claw is very good and well made. Like the other drop systems this claw uses a 2 button remote. It is also set up with a stepper motor with a screw for opening and closing the claw. This gives control on how much you open or close it.
The claw itself is larger and you will have to turn off the downward obstacle avoidance. Also while landing you will need a forward motion to avoid pressing up into the drone and offsetting it. It comes with a connected nylon cord to attach to the drone.
The good things:
Stepper motor is very strong and able to hold anything I have picked up with it.
Build quality is very good.
Remote uses a 9V battery and claw uses a rechargeable micro usb.
Things I would change:
I would change the frequency of the remote to 900 MHz to get a better distance.
I would offer an optional winch also controlled by the controller for lowering and raising the claw.
Is this worth the money?
If you are just going to use this to drop things then there are cheaper options out there. The nice thing with this is if you have something that needs to be recovered you can lower the drone over top it and pick it up.
The one main bad thing is the claw needs to be attached a fixed distance from the drone. So if you hang it to low the claw and its cargo swings around allot while you are flying. If you make the cable to short then you are risking the drone when lowering on top of what you are picking up. If you had a remote controlled winch you could lower the claw to pick up the cargo and raise it back up near the drone for a more stable flight.
Also the distance of the remote is very limiting. Don’t get me wrong it is useable up to about 300 feet but I think by switching to 900MHZ you should be able to get around 1000 feet with direct line of sight.
The shipment came directly from China and it took just about 2 weeks.

All and all it was pretty much what I expected, and if they come up with a remote controlled winch and a 4 button controller to use with this I would probably buy it.

review_body:
This is my first drone. I had $250 worth of Amazon gift cards that I had collected from Christmas and my 55th birthday and didn't need any golf stuff so i decided to look at drones. After 2 weeks of looking and reading reviews and watching a few videos, I decided to go with the Atom SE. It's a great drone. Very stable. Watch the many Youtube reviews of this drone and they are nothing but positive. I've had the drone for 3 weekends now and have flown it on 3 separate days. I had read the manual and watched a few tutorial videos before I flew it the first time. I flew it behind and over my house a few hundred feet above and beyond the house. It went perfect. Very easy to control and learn. The remote is awesome. I have a Pixel 7 Pro and it fits nice and snug even with a case on it. The batteries last quite a while, about 25 minutes on average. Today was the warmest day (45F) that I've flown it and the first time that the battery was warm enough to let me go into sport mode. Lots of fun flying around at 35 mph. The videos and pictures that I've captured thus far look a little bit better than the ones attached to Amazon reviews.

I did have a close call today. My oldest son and his fiance were visiting and I was showing my son the drone controls while it was hovering about 50 feet off of the ground. My controller started flashing warnings about losing signal and then the drone started doing a death spiral shortly after that. It started moving towards the ground in a spiral fashion and I got control of it with an emergency stop when it was about two feet off the ground. It was then that I remembered the iPhone warnings that I had heard about in the reviews. They say to put iPhones in airplane mode when flying the drone due to interference. My son had his iPhone in his pocket while I was showing him the controls. I had him place it in airplane mode after that and started the drone back up and flew it for about 15 minutes without issue.

Originally I purchased the 2 battery combo package but have since purchased the 3 battery charger with 1 additional battery. It's a great charger, easy to use and, fits nicely in the case. Speaking of the case, it's really nice and fits everything perfectly.

Overall, I think this is a great drone for the money. I have no regrets in purchasing it. My drone weighs in at 248 grams with the battery in it according to my weight watchers scale. If you're in the US don't forget to do your TRUST training. I did mine through the Pilot Institute website and it was very easy to complete.

review_body:
An update to this review concerning Potensic Support. As with any product new to the market I have experienced a few bugs with the Atom SE. The Potensic support team has worked with me on each of these issues and there have been a few firmware updates that greatly improve it's operation. Many of these have been at the suggestion of Atom SE owners. They listen to and welcome our input to improve their product. Most recently the onboard compass has apparently failed and my Atom crashed pretty hard. Support sent instructiions I followed but to no avail. Potensic has apologized for any inconvience and is replacing the drone under warranty. As I said at the end of my initial review the Potensic Support team is quite simply the BEST support staff I have dealt with in over thirty years. They stand behind their products and work with customers to keep us satisfied and flying. Thank you Potensic, you folks are great!!
I received my new Atom SE on Wednesday the weather was very overcast so I was only about to charge and start everything. Location, firmware update and time to fly. I am not easily impressed, but the short version of what I think of this drone, WOW! This drone flies amazingly well for one in this price range. Control inputs are instant, crisp, and very sensitive and took a bit of getting used to. Just basic maneuvers on the first day and it performs all of them extremely well.
The weather finally broke today (Sunday 1/15/22) and it was off to the park to put it through it's paces. Temperature was around 35 degrees F and brisk winds (Ground level 8-16 MPH) at around 80 ft. altitude wind gusted up to 32 MPH. It handles the wind better than I expected, it holds position and is stable except in the strong gusts. Even then it does move maybe 10 ft. when the gust stops it recovers right back to steady hover. Despite the cold and wind the battery life is almost dead on the rated flight time. I got 28 minutes of flying on the first battery with 10% left, the wind had increased a fair bit so the second battery flight time was 24 minutes with 10% left and considering how it fought the wind so well I am very, very pleased with flight time. Was great fun, but with a couple of extra batteries it will be a blast (sorry wallet).
Time to test the autonomous features. First the follow mode and it certainly does so. No matter the direction or number of direction changes it follows and keeps me in the frame. Circle mode is flawless and smooth (as my grampa used to say it's as smooth as the south end of a north bound baby). Waypoint mode again flawless, flies to each point smoothly and turns the corners crisply.
The best part of this little gem is the camera, it is amazing. It will record video at 4K 30FPS, 2.7K 30FPS, 1080P and 270P. The EIS gives you a very smooth video. The photos, well you can almost count the leaves on the trees and the colors are vibrant and sharp. A three axis gimbal and some more camera settings I think would give DJI Mini 2 a run for it's money.
In conclusion I am extremely happy with my Atom SE and highly recommend it especially for those who can't afford the likes of DJI or Autel. This is a very reasonably priced beginner to intermediate drone. I would love to see a three axis gimbal for even smoother and quality videos. Not to mention this is not my first Potensic drone and their support team is heads and shoulders above the norm, they are polite, prompt and most helpful. I give this drone five gold stars!

review_title: The Great Thing About This Drone Is It's Amazing and the Company and the People who Stand Behind It
review_body:
This drone is a great beginner or veteran drone that has most of the bells and whistles of very high priced drones. I selected it because I travel often and I like to travel light. This drone has amazed me at this price point with all of the features and reliability that it provides at the price point. My only desire was that perhaps I should have waited for the gimbal version, but then again I like the look of flying by the seat of your pants and this drone delivers.
It's a long story but I bought my initial drone and due to circumstances beyond my control it was lost and never to be found. I reached out to Protensic support who were very happy to discuss the matter with me and to work with me. I provided all of my data to them from the drone flight in which it was forever lost and they dove into it and found a way to make an improvement based on my data and in so doing offered to replace the drone for me as an act of appreciation for helping to improve the drone performance and control. In exchange of gratefulness I also provided them with a huge list of improvements, inventions, applications and ideas and concepts for future drone projects. We were all well pleased and they sent me my replacement drone as a courtesy. Last week I flew out to Utah for a week and I took it with me and I was able to fly and record in 4K such stunning scenery as lakes, rivers, mountains, meadows and even Bridal Veil Waterfall in Provo County. What a hoot! I advise to definitely keep it on training mode for a while to get very comfortable with it and be sure to try to keep it in site and to also keep an eye on the messaging on the phone screen. I had one instance in a highly magnetic area where I called the drone back to land at the starting point but in its journey back at 300 feet I received a notice that it was landing at a different point than the take off point. I was very concerned because of the huge lake and some other things in the area (I.E. a bridge and highway in the distance) but it all worked out well because I saw the message warning me and I was able to watch closely the screen the height, the heading, etc. and I was able to guide it in the final part of the return flight. This was an anomaly in an highly magnetic area but the warning gave me the heads up that I needed.
The person who worked with me in Customer Service was a jewel of a person who was kind, considerate, appreciative and was working in my best interest as well as the company. Its a rare thing to find these days in a company who will stand by their product. The drone is awesome and the company is awesome. I have zero regrets. I did learn to also write my name and phone number on my drone with a permanent marker, to put an extra air tag on it and to absolutely make sure I have sufficient satellites and that I let it hover on take off to fully announce that home base is locked into the auto return system.
I am one happy drone operator and I love that this one by weight requires no licensing. I may bump up the the gimbal control model but then again I can edit in my software to remove anything I want such as a crooked horizon. I also bought a take off landing pad, and a Mregh Solar Power Bank to recharge the batteries and controller on the go as well as extra memory cards.
The memory card purchase was a bit dicey for me as I don't know that much about memory cards and there are a ton of versions and specs, but you can just go by the basic specs and see what others have purchased or call and ask the company if more detail is needed. They love to hear from their clients.
Oh one thing more that I loved was that I had the very same tech support person via email the entire process of losing my first drone, sharing data, getting a review, getting a decision, receiving and setting up new drone. Same person, same great help. That's just cool. Oh I got a 8TB hard drive also because I love filming in 4K and it takes a good bit of data storage. As well a new laptop to remove files from my memory card while in the field.

review_body: Ok, so overall, for the price, I was impressed. Definitely a decent deal. That been said, let's get some things straight. First off, the range, which was my biggest concern, due to what I intended to use the drone for. The listing claims up to 13,000 ft range. While the drone may physically be capable of that, I would much more have appreciate that ŕthe seller clarifying the fact that without modifying or otherwise amplifying the controller's signal strength, realistically its closer to 1,200-1,500 ft with average obstructions (trees, buildings, etc.) And my highest observed range, with basically no obstructions, standing on a second floor balcony of a hotel, I think I saw close to 2,000 ft. Mind you I'm referring to distance from the controller at an average of 130 ft in height. And while it also claims the ability of very high heights, I have not exceeded the regulated 394 ft, in the interest of aerial safety. My other complaint, if you want to call it that, I'd say more of a "con", is build quality. I immediately had to have a new one sent because first flight I hit a neighbor's tree (not the drone's fault but mine for being high) and it completely disabled the camera. Without any argument, I received a replacement (not mentioning the whole tree or high parts, of course). Since then I've had no other incidents. The drone itself is still in good condition after over a month of having it. The controller on the other hand is now damaged. One antenna is cracked near the base, which doesn't appear to affect the performance at all but is a concern that it will eventually break off completely. And almost immediately, one of the screw-on joysticks broke off. Both of these things just seemed to happen easily while the controller was just sitting in the cab of my truck. In their defense, I'm not always careful with things and live a quite "rough" lifestyle, so it was likely my own fault, which is why I'm not deducting anything from my rating for that. The only other thing I find a bit inconvenient is the camera not having any sort of zoom. Not even digital. Just nothing. One fixed distance. Despite being able to pan anywhere between straight out ahead and straight down. I just have to come down a bit to see things in more detail. The picture is pretty good otherwise. So I'm giving it 5 stars because as I said, overall it's a decent deal. The thing is easy to fly and performs very well. All of the features that I have tried seem to work as stated. Battery life isn't too bad. I observe an average of 15 to 25 minutes per battery, which is pretty good compared to other drones I've had (that were all in this price range). Definitely recommend to anyone looking for a decent drone in this price range!

review_title: Some thoughts and a warning about refunds for this item.
review_body:
Warning, When you buy this you are not warned that this is under a new return policy if you should chose to return it. They will hold your money for up to thirty days or until they decide to take it off the container it is placed in when it hits their dock. This is not covered under their return when it is picked up by the carrier policy of pretty much everything else. They are apparently putting many items if not all over $100 or so ( I don't know the actual amount, they would not tell me) under this new wait for your money back policy.

The drone was good in the wind and even for most of its flight characteristics. The GPS functions and such are all pretty nice for a basic set.This drone is ok for the price if you are aware of the limitations of the camera system and some issues with phones and DJI mics effecting the range of the drone. Not using that mic and switching your phone into airplane mode can help. More below.

It can provide good pictures, if you have enough light and are willing to post process them to get the horizon back to level. There are only two directions you are getting a level horizon, straight into or out of the wind or breeze. That is the main drawback of the 2 axis gimbal. If you are okay with sideways pics your are good to go unless you run into the cameras other big issue, low light or high contrast will effect what I think is the electronic stabilization in a bad way. The picture may look good until you look at detail, then where you have contrast you may have a good view of the top of a building but a side in the shadows is blurred clear out and in such contrast to the clear parts the picture looks like a photoshop workup.

I had to re-calibrate the compass on every battery even from the same spot. If you do not calibrate it then this drone will start doing the toilet bowl self destruct procedure. For you new dronies that means the drone will start looping in an ever increasing circle wider and faster until it loses control and crashes into something and essentially self destructs.

The manual claims you only have to calibrate the compass once or if you move to another location about 50KM away from the last calibration point. This is something you should only have to do with a sub $50 drone in the first place but this one was requiring it every new flight after the first day..

I was having some interference lines go through the video at just 50 feet on a few occasions, they were becoming more common by 800ft. This was out in the country not anywhere near anything that should cause interference.

It is well known now this thing does not get along well with your phones that are required for video. The range and video transmission can be destroyed by using a specific DJI mic near you when flying, This has effected many social media reviewers and some don't yet know this is causing their distance issues. Another thing that will help is only flying in airplane mode on your phone.

I would love to try the new 3 Axis version of the Atom but it was not available on here when I ordered a mini 3 instead and now that it in stock is my money is still being held hostage so its not likely to happen any time soon. Since I bought the DJI mini3 in the mean time I am finding out they are not near as good at meeting their posted specs either but I would love to try the Atom 3X for a head to head vs the Mini 3 vs the value.

review_title: Awesome Customer Service! Great Beginner Quad Drone (With Camera / WiFi) for the Money!
review_body:
Thank you MocVoo / XUYIWEI Toys!

Quad Drone --

I bought the Mocvoo Quad Drone with camera because the price was very affordable and I could use it without much fear, to practice flying quad drones, increase my skill and confidence level. The quad drone is very easy to setup and very easy to fly. It has a decent size (about 8" - 9" diagonally measured), and has bright lights in the front and rear, which helps with knowing which way the drone is facing, for controlling it. It also has built-in Wifi (for connecting a phone - you download an App) and, yes, a manually adjustable camera. I set mine to look straight ahead. Through the App and your connected phone, you can make videos or take photos, and they are stored on your iPhone or Android.

The drone comes in its own semi-hard, padded carrying case with the quad, transmitter, 2 batteries, a USB charging cable, 4 blade protector / guards, some spare blades and a screw driver. Again, setup was easy - you simply unfold the quad's arms, charge the battery, and install 3 - AA batteries in the transmitter, and you're ready to fly.

Awesome Customer Service !!!
As I mentioned, I wanted this quad drone to practice with, as I am a beginner. On the 6th day of owning it, I took it out to fly and was up probably 60ft - 75ft, just hovering and looking at the horizon through my phone, when a still breeze came along. The quad started to drift and I became disoriented and lost control. The breeze carried the drone off and it flew away and was lost! My nephew and I searched for 2 hours in the park, and we were even able to reconnect to the quad drone's WiFi several times - I could even see video, but could not locate the quad. Finally I could no longer connect to the quad's WiFi, and it was lost.

I now had the case, accessories, transmitter, but no more quad. Thinking that I would need to purchase everything again, I contacted Mocvoo support and Xuyiwei Toys and explained what happened and asked it they could give me a discount on a new one. Well, to my joy and surprise, they offered to replace my quad drone at NO CHARGE!!! How awesome is that?!! My nephew and I are so happy! This is way beyond my expectations, and I will not hesitate buying other products from them! Thank You So Much!!

All in all, the DJI Mini 3 4K Fly More Combo with DJI RC strikes a great balance of performance, ease of use, and value. It’s a fantastic choice for hobbyists and content creators alike, and a solid step up from entry-level drones.

review_title: ★★★★★ Outstanding Little Drone – More Fun Than I Expected
review_body:
I already own two DJI Mini 4K drones, so I wasn't expecting the DJI Neo to impress me as much as it did. I purchased the drone-only version and after spending time with it both indoors and outdoors, I can honestly say this is one of the most fun drones I've ever owned.

The first thing that surprised me was how incredibly stable it is. Indoors, it hovers almost rock solid using its vision and optical sensors. Even in hallways and around the house, it feels confident and controlled. Outdoors, I flew it on a breezy day and was amazed at how well it held position despite not relying on the same GPS-based hovering that my Mini 4K uses.

The autonomous features are where this drone really shines. Follow Me mode works surprisingly well and feels almost futuristic. Watching the drone automatically track and follow me while keeping me centered in the frame was impressive. I even tested it on stairs and around obstacles, and it handled itself far better than I expected from such a small drone. It was really fun to walk down the street with this thing following me, watching the expressions of passerby's, looking at the strange looking object following me around like it was stalking me.

Another huge advantage is convenience. Unlike larger drones, the Neo is ready to fly in seconds. Hand launches, quick autonomous flight modes, and easy video transfers through the DJI Fly app make it incredibly easy to use. Because it has built-in storage, I was recording videos immediately without having to worry about memory cards.

Build quality is excellent, which is what I've come to expect from DJI. The fully enclosed propeller guards also make it much less intimidating for indoor flying and for beginners.

If you're looking for a traditional long-range aerial photography drone, DJI already has other models for that. But if you want a drone that is fun, portable, easy to use, great for tracking shots, and surprisingly capable both indoors and outdoors, the DJI Neo is an easy five-star purchase. It's like having your own invisible cameraman.

Highly recommended.

review_title: Great Value Compact Drone for Beginners and Casual Flying
review_body:
The DJI Neo 1 is a small and compact drone with a very good price-to-quality ratio. It’s an excellent option for beginners or for people who don’t need a large, complex drone or special permits. In my case, living in Colombia, drones under 200 grams do not need to be registered and are considered recreational, which makes this model even more attractive.

Despite its size, it offers decent image quality and useful features for casual flying. It’s lightweight, easy to transport, and very convenient to carry anywhere. Of course, we can’t expect a 30-minute battery life from a drone this size—the average flight time is around 14 minutes—so I highly recommend having at least three batteries for a better experience.

It’s important to understand that this drone has the DNA of more professional DJI drones, but it is not a professional drone in a small body. The image quality is good for its category, but one limitation is the lack of a more advanced multi-axis gimbal. Additionally, strong winds can affect stability when flying at higher altitudes.

Overall, it delivers exactly what it promises. It’s a very good drone that I would recommend both to beginners and to drone enthusiasts who want something compact, portable, and easy to use without taking up much space.

review_title: This is one of the best purchases I've made
review_body:
I’ve gone through a handful of drones trying to avoid spending big money. After losing a couple in the past, I tried to stay under the $1,000 mark. In order from cheapest to most expensive, I’ve owned the Ruko F11, SJRC F11, and HoverAir ProMax.

The Ruko and SJRC were exactly what you’d expect for the price: limited features, mediocre build quality, and not something you’d trust for anything serious. The HoverAir ProMax was the first one that felt like a real product, but it’s basically a selfie drone. It markets itself as a first-person drone with features like Follow-Me, but that mode barely worked. Even after spending extra on the controller, it constantly lost track of me. Between the drone and accessories, I spent around $1,000 and still couldn’t rely on it.

So when I picked up the DJI Neo, I wasn’t expecting much. I was wrong. It’s a fantastic drone.

The DJI Neo has many of the same features as the HoverAir, but there are trade-offs. The HoverAir definitely has sharper photo and video quality, and it has sensors on more sides. But the DJI Neo is half the price, and more importantly, it can be fully remote-controlled. With the DJI RC2 controller, I can fly it confidently across my entire 15-acre property, about a mile out, without issues. The HoverAir’s controller was limited to basic movement, maybe 100 feet of usable range, and constantly losing signal or tracking. One feels like a true drone, the other feels like a novelty item.

Yes, you sacrifice a bit of image quality with the Neo, but what you gain is a real drone experience: real range, real control, real reliability. Nothing kills the experience faster than constantly turning around on a trail to see if your drone stopped following you and then walking back 50 feet to retrieve it. I dealt with that constantly with the HoverAir. With the DJI Neo, that’s never been a concern.

If you want a dependable drone that actually flies instead of just hovering next to you for selfies, the DJI Neo is absolutely worth it.

I also wanted to be able to pluck the drone out of the air with my bare hands without having to worry that a gust of wind was going to result in my losing a finger. review_title: Disappointed with Neo - The Specs Fall Short
review_body:
I used the DJI Neo for a several hours the day it arrived and I can’t help but feel a little disappointed with the overall experience. It has its bright spots in the software capabilities and ease of use, but the video quality and tracking were no where near expectations. I have several 4K cameras, action cameras, drones, and this is NOT 4K video. More pros and cons listed below.

The Pro’s:
-Lightweight
-Easy to setup
-Software is really good

The Con’s:
-Video quality is not 4K
-Only shoots in horizontal, not vertical. Can’t believe it doesn’t have vertical video mode for posting on instagram/tiktok.
-The battery life is not as advertised. I used 80% of the battery and got 6.5 minutes of video using all the different automated modes (dronie, follow, rocket, etc). The Neo started with 95% charge and ended with 15%. This would give me about ~10 minutes of videos on a full battery. That is not anywhere near the 18 minutes that are advertised!
-Tracking from both front and back is not great. Often loses track if you take any type of hard turns.
-Downloading videos to phone is very slow without WiFi. Had to turn off my cellular (with full bars 5G) so it could download on WiFi only.
-The video is over sharpened and over saturated. This means objects look fuzzy in the background and colors look fake. For a “4K camera” that is not how it should look.
-The follow speed is quite slow (stated as 12mph). Anything more than a light jog and it will lose you. Can’t follow on a bike, scooter, or anything beyond a jog that well.

Overall, I feel DJI stretched the truth about the specs and performance of the Neo. I would rather pay more money for a real 4K camera that looks good, faster tracking speed, and better tracking capabilities. I love the experience of a flying camera and will be looking at other products that have better performance.

review_title: Extremely impressive you won't lose it
review_body:
Incredible drone! It’s unreal how I launched it off my building’s rooftop. The wind was strong up there, but the image was perfectly still. You couldn’t tell it was moving at all, like studio-quality film. I flew a couple of blocks away, all the way down to the wharf. There’s a hill and a bunch of buildings between me and the wharf. I ended up losing signal over the wharf and got scared. I thought I’d lose my drone, but it actually raised up in the air so high it went above the limit it’s usually allowed to go. It didn’t stop going up until it reestablished a clear connection with my phone and remote. I was able to fly back home without any problems. I was so relieved.

I could’ve stopped flying before it got out of reach. It was giving me serious indications that it was about to lose signal. It was flashing in and out and blinking that I was out of range, but I just kept pushing it anyway. I don’t know what I was thinking.

The drone is pretty friendly, very easy to use, and extremely portable. It’s very lightweight, and I actually put it in the pocket of my pants and rode my bicycle without even it being uncomfortable.

It’s also extremely durable. I crashed it once without blade protectors, and you couldn’t even tell that I wrecked it. There was only a small scratch on one of the blades.

The only function I wish it had was auto-tracking. It doesn’t auto-track a person or bicycle and follow you on its own.

review_title: Connection Problems and No Resolution from DJI
review_body:
I purchased this drone specifically for an important trip, and unfortunately it has been one of the most frustrating electronics purchases I have made.

The main issue is an intermittent connection problem between the remote controller and my phone. Sometimes everything works perfectly, but other times the phone fails to recognize the controller, disconnects unexpectedly, or loses connection during flight. What makes this especially frustrating is that the issue is sporadic and difficult to reproduce consistently.

I spent considerable time troubleshooting before contacting support. I tested multiple USB cables, multiple phones, and verified that the cables and phone ports were working properly with other devices. Despite all of this, the problem continued to occur.

At one point, the controller disconnected while the drone was in flight. I recorded the incident and provided video evidence, screen recordings, flight logs, and detailed explanations to support. I had already sent the drone and controller in for inspection once before, but because the issue is intermittent, the service center could not reproduce it and returned the equipment without resolving the problem.

Now I am being asked to send everything back again for another inspection that may take several weeks. Unfortunately, I purchased this drone specifically for an upcoming trip, and there is a real possibility that I will not have a functioning drone available when I need it most.

The drone itself has good image quality when it works, but reliability is far more important. A drone that may randomly disconnect from the controller or phone during operation is not something I can confidently recommend, especially considering the difficulty of obtaining a timely resolution through support.

Indoors feels a bit restrictive due to how responsive it is, so I’d recommend flying outdoors if possible. It did drift at first, but after adjusting it hovered very steadily. Battery life is short (about 10–15 minutes), but charging only takes around an hour.
The biggest downside is the camera quality, which is very low resolution. That said, I wasn’t buying this for photography, so it wasn’t a deal-breaker. I crashed it once and it held up fine. Overall, it’s worth the price and a fun way to learn how to fly a drone. Great for beginners, not for experienced pilots or anyone focused on camera quality. I’d buy it again or gift it.

review_body:
ORIGINAL REVIEW:

Was so excited to get this drone for my kids, good reviews, extra batteries (their micro drones gave only a couple minutes of fun before they died), good protection for the propellers (unguarded propellers on micros were constantly getting damaged and they had gone through all the extras that came with them w/no way apparently to get new ones). But out of the box the remote had an issue. Right joystick is sticky when you move it to the right. And by "sticky" I mean it gets stuck. I tried to work around it, but it's simply a no-go for something brand new. It goes zooming off in the direction that it is stuck and crashes. So sad to have the excitement of my kids ramping up and then come crashing down along with the drone. This one's heading back, though (since it came so fast and is relatively cheap) I'll probably try another one and hope for a good remote. Statistically speaking I shouldn't get a messed up remote twice in a row, right??

****** EDIT: (2nd drone) *******

So I did get a 2nd drone and can now give a slightly more informative review. I changed my rating to reflect my 2nd experience, though I think it's only fair to leave a quality control warning. My 2nd drone works fine, the remote isn't sticky and it does everything it is supposed to do. Having 3 batteries is great since they do run out relatively quickly (but not crazy fast), but the battery changing process is what makes this (to me) just a 4-star product. I know it's a micro drone so everything is small, but it's kinda hard to get the battery connector off of this thing. Might be in part because I have really big hands, but by design it is pretty hard to reach by where it is placed and the fact that the wires get in the way. The easiest way to do it would be to pull by the wires, but that goes against everything I was ever taught about unplugging things. And because you have to change batteries relatively frequently with this or any micro drone, this is a sore spot for me. Like I literally dread changing the batteries. Small-handed people may not have this issue, but it's very real for me.

Batteries aside, it's a fun little toy, easy to fly and the propeller guards do wonders - I have no doubt that they have kept this thing alive much longer than any other drones without guards since propeller damage is the #1 killer of drones. I think this is a great gift for kids or for bigger people wanting to learn how to wreck a drone without great financial impact.

review_body:
I was asked to be a tester for this drone. It arrived quickly and we were up and running in almost no time. After 1 flight, I lost the controls to my 8-year old who rapidly was hovering in no time.

Pros:
- I really like the packaging. It comes with a case to carry everything.
- Includes 2 batteries and 2 chargers. Great for charging 1 battery while flying on the othe
- Cartridge type batteries. I like that there was no opening hatches and pulling on wires/connectors to change out the battery. Just slide out one battery and slide in the new one
- Good battery life
- Fairly tough; survived 25+ crashes
- Easy to install iPhone app that was very intuitive
- Very fast compared to a couple of other drones we have. I played drone "chase" with my son and I could easily outrun his HS140.
- Folding arms/motor into a very compact form

Cons
- I prefer separate trim buttons. The remote has 1 trim button that puts the remote into trim mode. The joysticks are then used input the trim settings. The drone is uncontrollable while trimming. The trim mode does time out after about 2 seconds if there is no stick input. However, I had to get out of trim mode while still not trimmed out completely, just to get the drone back under control (especially outdoors with a little bit of wind).
- Very grainy video. HS140 seems to have a better camera, but it is also much bigger.
- The transmitter holder for phones did not fit my iPhone 7+ with a phone case installed. The holder is a spring loaded clamp where the clamp extends to get the phone in. It should extend a little more to accommodate larger phones.
- I don't like the pushbutton for transmitter on and off. With the door/phone holder closed, you can't tell if the transmitter is on. It does have different sounds for on and off. I prefer an on/off switch with a large LED like the HS140

We flew the drone a lot for about a week before it finally broke. I admit I crashed a few times, but my 6 and 8 year olds were very hard on the drone, as were some other children in the neighborhood. I was very impressed that such a small drone survived as long as it did. In the end, the plastic gear attached to the motor shaft spin and it appears that the inside of the gear is melted. I tried to take some pictures to see the damage. This was most likely the last crash where the motor was trying to spin the prop that was being prevented from rotating.

Conclusion:
I really like the drone. The advantages/features greatly outweigh the disadvantages/weaknesses. I do recommend this for more experienced drone pilots. It did not stand up too well to the abuse my young children provided. Great value/product for the price.

review_title: It is a flying drone in the first place
review_body:
I bought this product because I was always looking for a small helicopter or drone to fly around outside. The helicopters I tried in this price range had problems to maintain the position while hovering. So I was excited to try out this drone from DEERC.

Box Opening:
When it arrived, I noticed the clean look of the packaging for the D20. I appreciate that. Everything was well packaged and sitting tight in the respective places. It came with the drone, transmitter, 2 batteries, USB charging cable, 4 propeller guards, 1 set of replacement propellers, screwdriver, and manual.
Taking the drone out it felt that the quality for an pretty much all plastic device was decent. There is some extra plastic molding around the camera, but it does not impact the device performance. The transmitter is what you would expect for this price and it works fine.

Initial Setup:
We took everything out and followed the manual. Pairing the drone to the transmitter was easy and worked right away like a charm. I downloaded the app and had my phone connect to the drone’s access point. This worked but I had a more stable connection when I put my phone in airplane mode to make sure it would not switch between WIFI networks. Many phones nowadays are trying to give you an internet connect no matter what you do. The camera has 720p resolution and is fine and works but you cannot expect miracles.

Experience:
I stayed far below the max altitude of 131 feet but nevertheless it was fun flying around and doing circles. The drone responds quickly, and I had to practice a little to get used to the agility. I recommend starting outside or far away from valuables. Unfortunately, the camera disconnected every time right after the drone is up in the air. Also, it was challenging to keep it stable when it was in hovering mode even though I used the trim, and drone calibration. I crashed the drone in a bush once and it was still working fine. The battery life was great.

My summary:
This is a nifty little drone and is fun to fly around. The battery life is excellent. I decreased one star for the fact that it kept drifting off in hovering mode. The other star comes off for the app and the fact that it keeps disconnecting. If you just want a drone to fly around and do some spins this would do the trick in this price range.

I bought this mini drone for my kiddo (8 years old), and it has been a total hit. Setup was quick, it’s very easy to fly, and the 720p FPV camera makes it fun to see what the drone sees in real time. It’s the perfect mix of simple controls and features that keep kids (and adults) engaged.

First Impressions & Setup:
Right out of the box, everything was clearly labeled and intuitive. Charging the drone and controller didn’t take long, and the included instructions were easy to follow. My kid was flying within minutes, which was awesome — no complicated assembly required.

Flight Performance:
The controls are smooth and responsive, even for a beginner. Take‑off and landing are simple, and the drone stays stable in the air thanks to built‑in altitude hold. It handles basic maneuvers like forward/backward, left/right, and 360° flips with ease, which keeps flights fun.

Camera & FPV:
The 720p camera is really good for a mini drone in this price range. It streams video to the controller (or phone, depending on your setup), so we can see what it sees in real time — and that’s a huge highlight for kids. Photos and videos are decent quality for casual use and perfect for flying around the yard or park.

Durability & Safety:
It’s surprisingly sturdy. We’ve had a few minor bumps into trees and grass landings, and it held up well. The prop guards help protect both the drone and anything it might bump into — great feature for novices. It also has low battery alerts and an auto‑land function that makes it easier to prevent crashes.

Playtime & Battery Life:
Flight time is solid for a small drone — long enough to enjoy several flights before needing to recharge. The USB charging cable is convenient, and having spare batteries (if you get them) can extend playtime even more.

Pros:

Cons:

Who This Is Best For:
Ideal for kids, beginners, or anyone who wants a fun, easy‑to‑use drone with a camera that actually works. If you’re new to flying or want a safe first drone experience, this little quadcopter hits the sweet spot.

Final Thoughts:
This mini drone delivers way more fun than I expected for the price. It’s simple enough for kids to enjoy right away, but still exciting enough with its FPV camera and stable flight to keep older beginners entertained. Definitely a great pick if you want something that’s fun, functional, and reliable out of the box.

✔️ Highly recommend

Product Review for Amazon- HoverAir x1 white.

I am a new travel blogger and content creator. I am looking for a device that allows me to take drone-like images/videos, hand-free selfies, and fancy cinematic shots without using a DLSR Camera or a powerful lens.

I wasn’t sure about owning a drone as it is expensive and requires learning time.

So, I opted for HoverAir x1 as my entry-level - flying selfie camera/drone.

I have been using it for more than a month. Here is my feedback.

What I love about this product:

It is small and light. It can fit into the pocket of my yoga pants, the side of my backpack, and even my Chanel handbag.

The learning curve is not steep. You can get the concept after a few trials.

I like that it has a Storage Management system to keep all the shots I took; it allows me to view them before downloading them to my phone.

The Flight Mode fulfills most of my needs as a new travel blogger and digital content creator. There is Hover, which allows the device to hover while I am doing something like tying my shoelace, Zoom Out, which is great for establishing shots and also for group photos, Orbit, Bird’s Eye, Dolly, and more. They are enough to keep me busy and put together an excellent 30-second video on Instagram.

What is just ok about this product

Microphone … it is ok. I tried using my microphone … but it didn’t sound great. So I use voice over mic via 3rd party app to edit my footage.

Aerial View … I was hoping it could capture more surface, but then I realized it could fly up to 50 feet high.

Battery … It needs a recharge after about ten takes when I use the camera for both taking footage and viewing what I took. I could have taken more if I hadn’t viewed the shots I took.

Because this camera is light, it doesn’t do so well on windy days. It doesn't have the sensor system like a typical drone, so you can fly this in less crowded places and when the area is clear from cables, branhes, bushes etc.

What can be bothersome about this product

`1. It is noisy and loud. Not too lound but loud enough when I am out at 5 am to take shots or in a quiet area.

Despite my complaints, I’ve gotten used to this flying camera and love it. It is not a perfect drone-like camera, but it is perfect enough for me to get footage to put on social media. It is definitely not for professionals who need a robust drone camera, but it is suitable for beginners as well as DIY digital content creators who do not want to spend a dime on cameras and drones for their social posts.

Should you get it? I say yes if you are happy to be a non-professional videographer like I am.

review_title: If you need a reliable and accurate cameraman that fits in your pocket this the drone for you!
review_body:
I'm really just starting to work with this drone, but from what I've seen so far, this is an amazing piece of technology. I am so blown away by this little drone. It's really like having you're own personal cameraman and that cameraman can fly. Pros and cons:
Pros:
1. It follows you dutifully and in pretty difficult terrain. It is pretty hard if not impossible to lose once it locks on to you. I am really shocked at how good its optical tracking is. It's better than my Mini 4 pro on tracking people.
2. It is easy to use and requires no controller. Most of its functions are just a matter of pushing buttons on the drone itself.
3. Its hard to crash and pretty unflappable if it does hit something. If it makes a hard impact it just rights itself and lands. I put it into some small branches and it just pushed through. I hit a wall and it just landed. Its probably possible to crash it but I've not been able to yet. If it does crash it weights next to nothing and has a lot of semi rigid cage surrounding it to cushion the blow.
4. Its compact. You can carry this thing easily and it folds and unfolds instantly.
5. The video quality in good light is surprisingly good for 2.7k @ 30fps. It can shoot 1080p @30 or @60fps but I've not really used it yet to test how good it is. It always seems to be perfectly in focus and perfectly exposed. Also the image stabilization gimbal is first rate, it is a very smooth shooter.
6. You can use your phone to control its functions and it can use your phone to record audio which it automatically noise cancels the drones sound. Its pretty incredible. Sure, that can be done in post but this is just so easy to use and very effective. If you want to shoot and upload stuff immediately, this can do it.
7. It can download all the videos and photos you shoot to your phone and its very quick and easy.
Cons:
1. Battery life. The battery is small and light and it will give you anywhere from 10-20 minutes of flight time depending on how many demands you make in the way of movement. If its tracking you on a bike expect the low end of the scale, if it just hovering and tracking you, it will use less battery. The upside is you get 2 batteries with it, a very nice double charger and the small capacity mean they charge fast. I didn't time it but it seemed like about an hour to do the two batteries. The batteries are charged sequentially.
2. No 4k camera. That said, the camera is very good in descent light and starts to show some grain in low light but still not bad.
3. No removable SD card. It has 28gb of onboard storage if memory serves, which I've thus far come no where near using, but a removable card would be a nice touch.
4. No collision avoidance sensors. It is very good at following people, I used this in the woods that confounded my Mini 4 pro and was totally unflappable. It just sticks to you like glue and its so small it can really squeeze through tight spots. Granted the Mini 4 Pro is an all around great drone, super sophisticated, can do incredible things too, and its quite good at not running into things, but as far as being a close in robotic cameraman for shooting people, the Hover X1 is better. Turning corners in a house are probably its biggest struggle. That's where collision avoidance would be helpful. If it does hit a wall, it just lands itself so its not really a big deal.
5. No GPS positioning. All guidance is done via optical sensors. Whether its truly a con for the specific mission of this drone is debatable. It can operate in a building with ease as it doesn't need to connect to a satellite to be stable and follow your moves. It does need some light however to see you. If it cant see you, it just stops.
6. Range of operation. This drone is not going to fly more than whatever wifi range is. It is not intended to take high flying panoramic scenes. It is for shooting people relatively near the ground and it is very very good at it. If you need to fly far away this is not the drone for you. It does have very nice manual controls on the app with full flight control and gimbal control. It uses Wifi so while Ive not tested the limits of how far it can fly, it's going to be within Wifi range. That said, it doesn't require Wifi to do any of its major functions, only if you want to fly it manually.
7. Sound. Like any drone, its pretty loud and this thing whines like a giant swarm of mosquitoes. Of course it has the sound canceling so even though your talking in a what sounds like a banshee howl, your audio will come out pretty much pristine as long as you have your phone on you to use as a mic.

review_body: I am new to drones and this is my first one. I have flown it a few times now and it's really easy to use and has lots of features I never knew drones were capable of doing. I really like the auto tracking features, in which you can select an object (person) and have the drone follow it. The auto take off, return to home, and land are also features that are really cool. I am aware that most drones are capable of that. What really stands out are the sensors that provide 360 degree obstacle avoidance, as not many drones of this size have this feature. With recent firmware updates, you can actually "see" (in black and white) out of the 2 front and 2 rear sensors. This means if you're piloting the drone, you can swipe on the controller and pull up a window showing you what each of those sensors are seeing, one at a time. If you're going forward, you can pull up one of the rear sensors and see what's behind the drone. If you're going backward you can see what's in front of the drone. The controller with the built in screen is a nice touch, as you do not need to use your phone. The only thing I wish was better is the screen recording. When flying the drone, you record what the drone sees on either an SD card or the drone's built in storage. You can also record the controller's screen, which is a really cool feature. The controller has an SD card slot to do that, but it will not record the screen to the SD card even if you select it in the settings. Instead it saves screen records internally on the controller. To access those records, you'll have to hook the controller up to your computer. From what I understand, the controller can't record directly to the SD card due to bandwidth. Previous DJI control models recorded the screen as low res and was able to record directly to the SD card. The controller included in this bundle records the screen as hi res, which is too big to record directly to the SD card. This is a minor issue, but I thought I should bring it up. Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with this drone. I just wish I had more time and places to fly it.

review_title: Dangerous battery flaw, Retaining tabs on batteries are breaking off after only a few insertions

I noticed a battery seemed loose in the drone and after placing it in the DJI 3 port charger I noticed a retention tab was not coming back out. It was cracked, it broke off placing it back in the drone to get a cycle count (how many times it has been used.) That insertion made it cycle number 19, half of the previous insertions were just to get the endless updates they have had the last few months. The other tab is cracked and will break off next insertion, this will allow the batteries to fall out in flight causing a dangerous and potentially fatal scenario. I went online to find this was a common issue and happening far to often to some people

I contacted DJI, They will do nothing, the battery and drone has only a 15 day warranty. So you can figure it will cost you about $5 per insertion to own these junk batteries. The problem is the paper thin, brittle cheap plastic they are using to try to reduce weight, same with the drone, it is made with such a thin plastic if feels like it is cracking when you simply hold it. I replaced a Mini 3 with this drone, the Mini 3 felt and flew far batter than this Mini 4 Pro, this is jittery and jumpy in the air. It holds well in the air and the stabilization is great but this jumpiness in air is going to help throw these batteries with the breaking tabs out of the drone. We should not have to use tape to hold a battery in a $1200 drone after only a few flights. I should have stuck with a far cheaper drone, I was conned into the brand name equals quality scenario again and DJI has proven that a brand name and does not equal quality and you certainly do not always get what you pay for. They have some quality products to be sure, but I think they have reached the quality limit keeping it under the weight 250G limit. I can't imagine how far the Mini 5 quality will fall.

review_body: This is a powerful and functional little drone, if you keep its limitations in mind. I liked it so much I purchased 2 of them. The main app does not work, but you can find apps that do. This drone requires calibration everytime you power it on, it has no memory. The process is easy and take me under a minute. You run the ACC tool first while the drone is stationary on a level platform, then you run the compass calibration. Which involves physically spinning the plane in 2 different ways as shown in manual. Properly calibrated I had the drone up to 350 feet. The only time I had an issue is when the return to home function activated and it took one of the drones into a tree at 100 feet. I was able to retrieve drone it had not 1 scratch and runs the same as before. The theory is some sort of interference blocked the drone ability to get accurate gps data temporarily, as I was unable to get the drone out of RTH mode before it crashed itself. I would recommend taking the drone back down before 1/2 battery and would only push the drone to its limits on a full battery. If you are smart operator this is a nice little drone.

review_title: Excellent Drone with Incredible Performance and Flexibility
