I’ve owned several DJI drones, including the Mini 4K, and the Neo has quickly become one of my favorites.

The first thing that stands out is how responsive and dynamic it is. It’s fast, agile, and incredibly fun to fly. Whether I’m flying manually, using the joystick controller with the goggles, or taking advantage of the follow modes, the Neo feels very capable and versatile. The camera quality is excellent, and the footage has consistently impressed me.

Battery life is shorter than my Mini 4K, but that’s honestly expected given how much more aggressive and responsive the Neo is. You’re trading a little flight time for a much more dynamic flying experience, which is a trade-off I’m happy to make.

One thing worth mentioning is that DJI’s ecosystem isn’t always uniform across its drone lineup. Features like accessing recorded footage, retrieving goggle recordings, or syncing flight logs with third-party services such as AirData aren’t always handled exactly the same way from one DJI model to another. From my research, that’s more of a DJI infrastructure and software ecosystem issue than a problem with the Neo itself. Once you understand the workflow, it’s a minor inconvenience at most.

What I appreciate most is the flexibility. I can use it as a simple recreational drone, enjoy the follow-me features, fly it manually, or pair it with goggles for a completely different experience. It offers multiple ways to fly depending on what you’re trying to accomplish.

Overall, I’m extremely happy with this purchase. Right now I use it recreationally, but I also plan to incorporate it into my professional work. For anyone looking for a compact, capable, and highly enjoyable DJI drone, I would absolutely recommend the Neo.

To recap, can't think of one thing negative to report on this one. At $599 it was too hard to pass up.

review_title: Fun Little Drone with Smart Modes and Impressive Tracking
review_body:
I use the DJI Neo primarily for making content on trails and showing where I’m at in the world. It’s a compact, fun little drone with great automated modes that make it easy to get professional-looking footage without much setup. One of the things I really like is that it will literally fit in your pocket. That means I can take it anywhere without advertising that I have a drone in a public setting.

The follow-me mode works perfectly, keeping me centered and moving smoothly through the shot. The three-battery combo is a big plus, giving me plenty of flying time. Each battery lasts around 30 minutes in calm conditions, though that drops in windier weather. This drone doesn’t do great in strong winds and doesn’t have any obstacle avoidance, so it’s best suited for open trails or beaches. On the plus side, it will retrace your path accurately—if you walk around a pole, it will fly around that pole.

I use Dronie mode all the time, and Circle and Boomerang are great for dynamic shots. Helix is fun for stationary scenes. Just know that if you are trying to be stealthy, you're not.

I also use my Avata 2 goggles and hand controller with it, which work great together. Indoors, it’s stable enough but not perfect. You’ll want calm conditions and smooth control movements. I haven’t tried it yet with my e-bike, but based on how well it tracks, I think it’ll keep up just fine.

Pros:
Fits in your pocket for easy carry
Excellent automated flight modes
Accurate tracking and path memory
Great for creating travel and outdoor content
Works well with Avata 2 goggles and motion controller

Cons:
No obstacle avoidance
Struggles in windy conditions
Not very stealthy due to the sound level

Summary:
This drone is a fun, creative tool for content makers who want cinematic shots without the bulk or hassle of larger drones. It’s pocket-sized, easy to fly, and performs beautifully in calm conditions. Perfect for trails, travel, and quick content creation.

review_title: Childhood Dream Achieved - Flying Like A Bird!
review_body:
I just got to fly the DJI Avata 2, and dude, it’s so much fun. If you’ve ever been curious about flying FPV drones but felt kinda intimidated by all the gear and setup, this one’s for you.

So, first off, it comes with these goggles (DJI Goggles 3) that are super comfy and give you that full-on immersive flight vibe — like, you feel like you’re actually in the sky. And instead of the typical drone controller, it uses this motion-sensing thing called the RC Motion 3. You basically point where you want to go. It sounds gimmicky, but trust me, it just works. After a few minutes, you’re swooping around like you’ve done this for years.

The camera on it is insane for how small the drone is — it shoots in 4K, and the footage looks chef’s kiss. Super wide angle too, so everything feels big and dramatic. It even does slow motion if you want to get those buttery cinematic shots. And it’s got a ton of internal storage, which is awesome if you’re like me and forget to bring SD cards half the time.

What really got me though is how beginner-friendly it is. There’s this Easy ACRO mode that basically lets you do flips and rolls just by pressing a button. It makes you look like a pro, even if you’ve never flown an FPV drone before. And if you're worried about crashing — don’t. It’s built like a little tank with propeller guards and all, so it can take a few hits while you're getting the hang of it.

The only thing that might be a small downside is that the simulator support isn’t amazing yet, so if you’re someone who wants to practice a lot virtually first, that’s something to keep in mind. But honestly, it’s forgiving enough that you could learn on the fly (literally).

If you’ve been on the fence about getting into drones or FPV in general, the Avata 2 makes it feel way less scary and way more fun. It’s like DJI made it for people who want the thrill without the stress.

review_title: Fun, but it definitely has issues
review_body:
First thing I did with this was find the most open area that existed on the farm. My property is 500 acres of former farm, but the problem is it hasn't been a farm since 1945ish. That means woods. Lots of woods. I already lost one weird little cheap drone because the controls were awful, it weighed an ounce and a light breeze blew it somewhere into the trees. So, with this one, I went close to my house, but not close enough to get into the power lines. Turns out that was a pretty good idea because the phone app is kind of a joke. I tried to use it to control the drone, and it lost connection at what couldn't have been more than 150 feet. The video cut out and I just completely lost signal altogether. The control still worked fine though. The video it does take is kind of hilariously bad. You know those security cams that advertise 4k but somehow look worse than a camera phone from 2006? Yep. That. If you're new to drones and you've watched amazing footage on YouTube or wherever of drones taking professional quality video...uh...this isn't that. I can't knock it too much for that though. The drones you see taking those great videos are much, MUCH more expensive that this.

My S21 Ultra won't fit in the phone holder in its otterbox. That's annoying, but not surprising. The controls for this are very weird. They are analog sticks, but they operate like digital buttons. In other words, on/off. A little bit of input is the same as all of the input. That's fun. Battery life is kind of bad. Don't touch sport mode. It drains the battery in five minutes. I mean, you'll go up and it will be doing an emergency, kamikaze landing before you know it.

Once you get the hang of the awkward controls and don't put it in sport mode, it is fun. The GPS thing is nifty. I set it up to fly around the open area of the farm and stop at various waypoints. My kids chased it around the whole time it was doing that. The whole time was maybe 20 minutes. It then ran out of battery again. Up to 60 minutes flight time seems a tad optimistic.

I almost gave this 4 stars, but that awful battery life really made me think it was worth closer to 3. You might think of this as somewhere around 3.4 stars. 68/100 on that scale if that makes more sense. It's not terrible for the price, but it really has issues.

review_title: Very functional adult type drone that’ll provide the fun and experience at a reduced cost.
review_body:
The F28 Pro Foldable Drone from Contixo, is a very usable drone on the lower end of the spectrum for real 4k adult style drone. It’ll provide a great experience for those that are new to drones or if you just want a capable drone, for a fair price. Here are some of the things I’ve learned while owning it and things to consider before buying.

I. Quality – Its decent quality for a drone at this level of cost. All the parts seem durable enough to survive most non-catastrophes and should hold up well if you can keep it from running into too many things. I’d put it in the middle level of the quality scale for drones.
II. Usability – I found this to be on the level of an adult drone and not the best choice for a kid. This company offer better choices, if this is for a kid. The controls were easy to use and somewhat intuitive, but a little difficult to get used to. It’s set up to be adequate for a complete beginner, but the lack of propeller guards could be costly depending on your natural skills.
III. Features – This drone offers some great features for the price that work pretty good considering the cost. The 4K camera is viewable through my phone, and has been functional and worked well. Return to home, waypoints, one-key spiral, and follow me modes are all nice features to have in this class, although somewhat standard now.
IV. Package and Accessories – It comes with a good starter package with a pretty nice case that has a spot for everything and two batteries that last about 20 minutes each. Unfortunately, additional parts seem to be unavailable in their store at the time of writing this.

Overall, this has been a fun drone to use and I’ll continue to enjoy it for certain experiences. I’d recommend it to anyone looking for a starter adult type drone or if you just want to have fun with one without the worry of damaging a higher priced version.

You can trust that this review is simply my honest opinion that is attempting to provide you with helpful insight that I wish I had before I picked this product. Hopefully it was helpful in your decision.

review_body:
This is a butane fogger, a "thermal fogger" that heats up the chemical you are spreading, mixed with an oil, to fog with fine droplets. The other type of thermal fogger is a propane fogger. And there are also cold foggers that don't use heat.

A propane fogger works by burning propane that heats up the chemical mixed into an inert oil, spreading the chemical droplets around.
A butene fogger, by my understanding, uses the butane (a much tamer fuel than propane) as an igniter to burn a flammable oil such as diesel, and most of the burning is done by the diesel. This may stink, but it can produce the finest droplets. Since diesel or other flammable fuel was burned, less of the butane is used -- compared to a propane fogger where the only thing burned is the propane. This was my understanding, and I think it's supported by various online videos and explanations.

Now when I read the instructions for the BY-200 Compact Fogger I am reviewing here, it said that only inert oil should be used. I checked this with the seller, and the seller replied "You should not use diesel or fuel oil with the BY-200. This unit is designed for precision backyard and garden applications, and using diesel can create dangerous fire hazards, thick toxic smoke, and damage the internal components of this specific lightweight model."

It seems a standard butane fogger to me and I don't know why its internal components would be more vulnerable to damage from burning diesel than others, but the seller does not approve that use of the fogger. So this butane fogger is designed for precision applications rather than spreading smoke around in a large area, as with most thermal foggers including butane foggers. If you use a flammable oil in the tank, it's at your own risk.

It seems to be a well made fogger, but it's approved only for limited use by the seller and according to the instructions. Thus I cannot go higher than four stars.

review_title: A Great Drone for Me and the Girls
review_body:
I picked up this Contixo drone to have some fun outside with my two daughters, who are 11 and 13. I wasn't looking to become a professional photographer, just wanted something that worked well and wouldn't be a huge waste of money. I'm giving it a full five stars because it hits that sweet spot perfectly and has been a ton of fun for all of us.
The best thing about this drone is the GPS. The "return to home" feature is fantastic. If the girls fly it too far or we get nervous, one button brings it right back to where it took off. That feature alone takes a lot of the stress out of flying. It's also surprisingly stable in a light breeze, which I credit to the brushless motors. It feels like a solid piece of equipment, not a flimsy toy. The fact that it folds up and fits into its own sturdy carrying case is a huge plus, and not needing to register it with the FAA saved me a headache.
As for dislikes, the 2K camera is just okay. It's clear enough for us to get some cool shots of the house and the backyard, but you won't be filming any nature documentaries with it. The video quality is decent for the price, but not mind-blowing. Also, getting the app on my phone synced up took a minute; my daughters, of course, had it figured out instantly.
For the price, this drone is an excellent value. It’s a major step up from the cheap drones you see in toy stores, but it doesn't have the intimidating price tag of the high-end models. It’s the perfect machine for a dad who just wants to get outside and make some cool memories with his kids. It does exactly what I wanted it to do, and we've had a blast with it.

review_title: It's not particularly good at anything
review_body:
I've flown super high end camera quadcopters to 100+ mph racing quadcopters so I have a lot of experience in this realm. Granted those two are a bit off the spectrum, I also use another, more middle of the road $400 camera quadcopter for basic video stuff. They all have their place, every price point and use case. This one, on the other hand, doesn't really fit into any place at all. It isn't really good at any of the things that it is designed to do.

To start, the camera is terrible. It's very red-washed and has very little in the way of color reproduction. Everything is very, very red and not in the warm color tone kind of way, but it's like the camera is broken. Everything's some sort of pinkish variation of what it actually is in real life. It is just an incredibly bad camera that sacrifices everything that actually matters in order to put a bigger number in the resolution field of the marketing material.

The software that runs the quadcopter needs serious tuning. Going from a stop to moving is fine, but going from moving to stopping is a wild experience. Instead of gracefully slowing down this thing yanks in the opposite direction rapidly and it makes it hard to fly. It also cannot tolerate light wind as most others do, it is as if it is incredibly over-tuned and overcorrects for everything. It's very jittery and jarring overall.

The smart phone side of the software is also similar in that it is super jank. You don't connect to it via the software, you have to back out of it, connect to the quadcopter's wifi hotspot, come back to the app and patiently wait for it to connect and pray it works the first time otherwise you will be restarting the process a few times over as I have to do every single time. If you're lucky enough to get it connected you have to say another prayer that the video feed comes in with it because 50% of the time it does connect it has no video and you have to start the process again... again. It's an endless loop.

Once it does connect most of the important things are easy to get to: flight modes, flight settings, camera settings, etc. That is all fairly straightforward, but despite the app automatically formatting the SD card no videos or pictures actually show up on the SD card. I recorded a handful of videos to demonstrate the issues I was having with it and I have not been able to get a single one to any device, be it my phone or my computer. I tried it with a 32GB and 64GB SD card, both in good working order, to no avail. They show up on the device, but not on the card and that is the only way to transfer them.

The quadcopter and transmitter are also super cheap. The plastic is terrible quality, creaky and feel horrible in the hand. The transmitter is extremely top heavy with the phone installed into it and it is incredibly uncomfortable to use. The only support you have for the bottom half of it is two little legs that fold out and they are constantly digging into your fingers with the weight of the phone pushing up from the weight of it pulling down at the top.

I don't know. It's cool - if any of it worked even remotely "okay" it would be a viable option. A $150 camera quadcopter that isn't just actual e-waste, but decent enough to mess around with it would be fine, but it's just really bad at everything. I grabbed this with the sole intention of having a cheap one on hand for looking for lost model airplanes and not being out a ton of money should the quadcopter get lost, but it is such a pain to use I almost feel better off just spending the time I would trying to get this to work walking the field.

This is a cheap toy at best and an outright scam at worst. I'll give it two stars for coming in a nice case.
